Find out the circumstances of the bite and first aid given.","After examination, reassure the parent that the wound needs only cleaning and closure, and explain how you will do this.","Antibiotics are not necessary \u2013 low risk of infection (e.g., a recent wound, the face has an excellent blood supply, etc.).","Check on the child\u0027s tetanus immunisation status and explain whether a booster is needed (NOTE: Australia is free of rabies).","Advise the parent on care of the wound \u2013 recommend a review after 48 hours.","Advise on the need for constant supervision of children near dogs."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 50-year-old insurance broker whose recent divorce has been stressful and wants a holiday to restore energy and spirit.
Background: Your patient is a 50-year-old insurance broker whose recent divorce has been stressful and wants a holiday to restore energy and spirit. However, the company boss has refused a request for vacation leave. Your patient has come to see you today to request a medical certificate that will allow him/her to have two weeks off work.
TasksJson: ["Refuse to issue a medical certificate as your patient is not depressed.","Explain that issuing a deliberately false or misleading certificate represents professional misconduct.","Emphasise that misuse of sick leave is a serious matter (e.g., going on vacation while pretending to be sick might have consequences if the boss should question the medical certificate).","Acknowledge that stress affects health and try to convince him/her to see a psychologist for stress management by emphasising the long-term benefits of therapy."]

ScenarioTitle: This 65-year-old retired academic opted for early retirement because he/she was finding it difficult to manage his/her workload.
Background: This 65-year-old retired academic opted for early retirement because he/she was finding it difficult to manage his/her workload. There is a fairly strong history of early-onset Alzheimer's disease in his/her family. The patient has come to discuss the possibility of genetic testing with you.
TasksJson: ["Ask the patient if he/she has any questions about dementia generally, and if the patient is familiar with the symptoms of Alzheimer\u0027s.","Discuss the possibility that the patient may be experiencing other forms of impaired cognitive performance, such as depression.","Persuade the patient to see a clinical neuropsychologist before considering having genetic testing and explain the reason for this (e.g., formal cognitive evaluation and assessment of the possibility of depression as a component, etc.).","Explain that prior to any future genetic testing, the patient will need to have specialist genetic counselling (counselling from health professionals with specialist training in genetics and counselling) to consider possible outcomes of the testing."]

ScenarioTitle: An overweight 76-year-old patient is seeking advice about hip pain.
Background: An overweight 76-year-old patient is seeking advice about hip pain. He/she has experienced worsening pain in the right hip for a number of years. Lately, he/she has begun using a walking stick for support for everyday movements and activity. He/she is anxious about possible reasons for the increased pain and likely treatment recommendations. Be reassuring.
TasksJson: ["Explain possible causes of the symptoms: various, including osteoarthritis (most likely), bursitis, tendinitis, referred pain from back.","Give reasons for the worsening symptoms (e.g., cause remains untreated, etc.).","Inform the patient that hip pain is quite common in people over 65; most common cause is arthritis.","Explain that physical examination and X-ray (for arthritis) are required for diagnosis.","Discuss treatment options: depends on diagnosis (for arthritis \u2013 weight loss, modification of activity, paracetamol, NSAIDs, physiotherapy, referral for hip replacement if conservative treatment fails).","Tell the patient what happens now: diagnostic examination/X-ray; follow-up to confirm diagnosis, treatment plan and treatment monitoring."]

ScenarioTitle: This 29-year-old lawyer has been experiencing heart palpitations.
Background: This 29-year-old lawyer has been experiencing heart palpitations. The patient is extremely busy, eats fast food very often and consumes large amounts of coffee. Both his/her physical examination and ECG are normal.
TasksJson: ["Ask the patient about his/her heart palpitations.","Suggest that the patient\u0027s symptoms could be caused by stress and anxiety.","Empathise with the patient\u0027s situation but inform him/her that the symptoms are not due to coronary problems (e.g., ECG and physical exam normal, etc.).","Give suggestions to help the patient manage the heart palpitations (e.g., stress management, reduction in caffeine intake, etc.). Include a healthier diet as a suggestion.","Recommend ways of eating healthier (e.g., making healthier choices in restaurant, etc.) and explain that these are important for long-term health."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 49-year-old accountant, diagnosed six months ago with rheumatoid arthritis (RA).
Background: Your patient is a 49-year-old accountant, diagnosed six months ago with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). The symptoms of joint pain and fatigue have been well-managed with NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs), but one week ago, he/she experienced a ‘flare’ (period when joints are more inflamed and painful). The patient smokes 10 cigarettes per day. He/she is seeking your advice on the anticipated course of the illness and appropriate management.
TasksJson: ["Explain that RA is a chronic disease, which will not just \u2018go away\u2019 (e.g., no cure, remits and relapses, current flare will probably settle but more quickly with medication, etc.).","Provide strategies for coping with RA (e.g., rest, sleep, modify diet, sensible exercise \u2013 long walks, massage, hot treatment, etc.).","Provide reassurance \u2013 early diagnosis and intervention are important for improving patient outcomes.","Advise the patient to stop smoking.","Offer to refer the patient to a rheumatologist for specialist advice and possible cortisone treatment."]

ScenarioTitle: This 64-year-old patient is planning a holiday overseas and has come in for a medical examination required for his/her travel insurance.
Background: This 64-year-old patient is planning a holiday overseas and has come in for a medical examination required for his/her travel insurance. You are surprised to find his/her blood pressure is 190/110.
TasksJson: ["Express your concern at such a high blood pressure reading and explain that the condition increases the risk of stroke and heart disease.","Question the patient about his/her lifestyle: smoking, alcohol, diet, stress factors, etc.","Explain that medication may be needed and that other measures should be taken (looking at diet, exercise, etc.) to bring the blood pressure down.","Explain that you will arrange further tests \u2013 ECG, cholesterol, urinalysis (as there may be a treatable underlying cause, such as renal or endocrine disease; heart disease is also a concern). While the problem might be stress-related, you cannot impose treatment based on a single reading.","Reassure the patient that he/she will still be able to go on holiday."]

ScenarioTitle: You are speaking to a parent of a three-and-a-half-year-old boy.
Background: You are speaking to a parent of a three-and-a-half-year-old boy. The parent has two older children who had no problems with toilet training but the youngest has not been successful. He/she is worried this may be a symptom of a more serious condition.
TasksJson: ["Explain to the parent that his/her son is still young and encourage him/her to be patient (e.g., probably not quite ready yet, etc.).","Ask if the boy has any other symptoms (e.g., irregular bowel movements, stomach pains, constipation, etc.).","Reassure the parent that later toilet training is not abnormal and ask what techniques he/she has been using to toilet train the boy.","Suggest some alternative techniques (e.g., a reward system, involving the older children, do not punish or nag the child, discuss toilet training with the child using books, videos, etc.).","Reassure the parent that his/her son will pick up the necessary skills when he is ready."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 54-year-old widow/er with advancing motor neurone disease.
Background: Your patient is a 54-year-old widow/er with advancing motor neurone disease. The son wants to become your patient's enduring medical power of attorney (MPOA), someone who makes medical treatment decisions for a person should that person lose the capacity to make those decisions. Your patient is not close to his/her son, feels pressure to appoint him as MPOA, and wants advice.
TasksJson: ["Explain that it is not necessary to appoint a MPOA and he/she can appoint someone other than his/her son.","Provide reassurance \u2013 no one can appoint themselves as MPOA for another person. The patient must have the capacity to understand the implications and consequences of appointing MPOA (otherwise it is not legally valid).","Reassure the patient that he/she will be supported during illness (MPOA cannot arrange euthanasia or refuse palliative care).","Offer to prepare an advance care plan for the patient so he/she can document his/her end of life choices; ensure he/she has a will."]

ScenarioTitle: This 63-year-old patient is enquiring about the need for a tetanus vaccination.
Background: This 63-year-old patient is enquiring about the need for a tetanus vaccination. He/she cut his/her right foot while working in the garden recently. He/she cleaned the wound but is worried about contracting tetanus.
TasksJson: ["Find out the reasons for the patient\u0027s enquiry.","Check for any symptoms of tetanus \u0027lockjaw\u0027 (e.g., muscle stiffness and spasms in the neck, especially a stiff jaw, 4-21 days after injury).","Explain why tetanus is a serious disease (e.g., affects nervous system, muscles, etc.).","Reassure the patient that the consultation was a good idea (booster required every 10 years: immune system may not work as well with age). Recommend a tetanus vaccination if required (if previous vaccination was more than ten years ago, advise the patient to have another booster).","Encourage the patient\u0027s gardening hobby (outdoor exercise).","Advise on suitable footwear to avoid future gardening injuries (strong, covering the feet, thick soles, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: This 23-year-old student presented a week ago complaining of tiredness.
Background: This 23-year-old student presented a week ago complaining of tiredness. He/she described difficulty getting to sleep and stress over upcoming exams. He/she has had no other symptoms and is not clinically depressed. Examination last week was completely normal. You ordered some basic blood tests and the results are all normal.
TasksJson: ["Reassure the patient that there is no major medical cause for his/her symptoms.","Explain that stress from exams and poor sleep are the likely causes of the symptoms.","Suggest regular gentle exercise and avoidance of stimulants like coffee and sugary foods; encourage him/her to find time to relax.","Explain that you cannot write a medical certificate for a time in the future.","Find out about his/her concerns about exams and respond sympathetically.","Suggest that he/she try your recommendations and come back next week so you can review how he/she is getting on."]

ScenarioTitle: This 27-year-old patient is presenting with a painful, red and swollen 2cm cut on his/her upper left thigh.
Background: This 27-year-old patient is presenting with a painful, red and swollen 2cm cut on his/her upper left thigh. Three days ago, the patient fell and cut his/her thigh on a piece of metal. You have examined the cut and determined that it is infected and will require treatment.
TasksJson: ["Ask if the patient has taken anything for the wound, applied any medications to the area, and if the patient has been immunised against tetanus.","Explain that the cut seems to be infected and will require treatment (e.g., antibiotics, etc.).","Convince the patient that it is necessary to clean the wound and give reasons why (e.g., foreign bodies present, etc.).","Suggest another tetanus injection as the last dose was a long time ago.","Explain that you want to see the patient tomorrow to review the wound, and that if it continues to deteriorate, surgical debridement (e.g., removal of unhealthy tissue, etc.) might be necessary."]

ScenarioTitle: You see a 45-year-old patient who suffered a mild anterior acute myocardial infarction two weeks ago.
Background: You see a 45-year-old patient who suffered a mild anterior acute myocardial infarction two weeks ago. Recovery was uncomplicated and the patient was discharged from hospital four days ago. He/she is now concerned about how much physical activity is appropriate during recovery.
TasksJson: ["Find out reason for visit.","Reassure patient about fatigue (e.g., expected: 4\u20136 weeks for return of full energy levels, etc.). Remind patient about heart attack recovery (e.g., gradual, lifestyle changes and medication to help, etc.). Emphasise importance of exercise (e.g., heart health: strengthening heart; overall health: lowering cholesterol; etc.).","Give recommendations for exercise (moderate physical activity: patient\u2019s recovery uncomplicated, already two weeks since hospital admission, etc.). Advise importance of joining cardiac rehabilitation programme (e.g., increasing exercise tolerance under supervision, etc.). Explore patient\u2019s job (type of work, etc.).","Give timescale for return to work (e.g., 4\u20136 weeks for desk job, etc.). Explain need to be physically and emotionally ready (e.g., not rushing back, planning return to work: assistance/support from employer, etc.). Explore any concerns.","Provide recommendations for prevention of future attacks (diet: vegetables, whole grains; lifestyle: physically active; etc.). Reassure patient about his/her concerns (e.g., normal, appropriate, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: Your 41-year-old patient has come for a review appointment. The patient was recently diagnosed with bipolar disorder (a psychiatric conditio
Background: Your 41-year-old patient has come for a review appointment. The patient was recently diagnosed with bipolar disorder (a psychiatric condition characterised by extreme mood changes). He/she has been prescribed sertraline (Zoloft) and his/her condition has stabilised. The patient wishes to discontinue treatment.
TasksJson: ["Discuss how the medication is working.","Ensure the patient has not been experiencing trouble sleeping, suicidal thoughts or other potential side effects.","Explain the importance of continuing to take the medication as prescribed (e.g., stopping medication can cause return of symptoms, etc.).","Try to convince the patient to continue the treatment (e.g., medication appears to be working, etc.).","Reassure the patient, who is anxious that people will think differently of him/her if they find out about his/her bipolar disorder."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 58 year old company accountant with a demanding job.
Background: Your patient is a 58 year old company accountant with a demanding job. He/she is overweight and doesn’t exercise regularly. Recently, your patient has been feeling unusually tired, has lost a few kilograms and his/her vision is a bit blurry. The patient feels overworked and thinks the long hours on the computer are causing eye strain and he/she needs reading glasses. Your patient’s spouse urged him/her to see the doctor about the eye issues.
TasksJson: ["Explain that the blurred vision might be caused by diabetes.","Recommend tests for diabetes (including on-the-spot random blood glucose finger prick). Reassure the patient that the tests are straightforward.","Explain why you think it might be diabetes (positive risk factors: history of being overweight, inactive, recent onset of lethargy, blurred vision and weight loss).","Recommend a referral to an ophthalmologist. Try to convince the patient to undergo testing for diabetes."]

ScenarioTitle: You are working at a suburban medical clinic. A parent has returned to receive results of an ultrasound performed by his/her 8-year-old daug
Background: You are working at a suburban medical clinic. A parent has returned to receive results of an ultrasound performed by his/her 8-year-old daughter yesterday. The child had presented with vague abdominal pains of several weeks' duration and on examination you felt a right loin mass, which is why you ordered the ultrasound. The ultrasound shows that the child has Wilms' tumour (kidney cancer) and needs to be seen by a specialist urgently.
TasksJson:
["Be sympathetic and reassuring to the parent. Give him/her the following information:
- The results have been received and the news is not good.
- They indicate that the child has kidney cancer (Wilms' tumour).
- This form of kidney cancer is the most common seen in children, and can be effectively treated in most cases, with a good prognosis.
- The child needs to see a specialist (paediatric oncologist) as soon as possible to devise a treatment plan.
- Tell the parent you will arrange an appointment with a specialist straight away."]

ScenarioTitle: A fifty-year-old patient has come to see you for a routine health check.
Background: A fifty-year-old patient has come to see you for a routine health check. You notice that he/she has gained a lot of weight since last presenting. You discover that his/her BMI is 35 (obese). You know this patient has a family history of heart disease, and that his/her father died suddenly of a heart attack in his fifties.
TasksJson: ["Find out about diet and lifestyle factors; investigate any possible psychological issues.","Convince this patient that he/she must lose weight.","Suggest lifestyle changes the patient can make to facilitate weight loss (e.g., exercise, change diet, etc.). Accept no excuses regarding sedentary work routine or limited mobility.","Impress upon him/her the risks associated with obesity (e.g., cardiovascular disease, diabetes type II etc.).","Suggest a referral to a dietitian, or possibly a psychologist."]

ScenarioTitle: A middle-aged patient has presented with an episode of transient unilateral weakness of the arm with sudden onset.
Background: A middle-aged patient has presented with an episode of transient unilateral weakness of the arm with sudden onset. It was accompanied by dysphasia. You examine the patient, including carotid auscultation, heart rate, blood pressure and respirations. Explain that the problem may be related to the heart or blood vessels, but you want to do more tests to exclude a transient ischaemic attack (TIA: often known as "mini-stroke").
TasksJson: ["Find out the history of the symptoms and how long the episode lasted.","Explain the need to order blood tests - full blood examination, thyroid function tests, blood glucose and cholesterol, urea and electrolytes, creatinine clearance.","Refer the patient for a CT scan and ECG.","Explain to the patient, without alarming him/her, that TIA must be ruled out.","Answer his/her questions about other possible causes and how to prevent recurrence or serious complications."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 26-year-old student who returned from an overseas vacation recently.
Background: Your patient is a 26-year-old student who returned from an overseas vacation recently. The patient has felt as though he/she has had flu symptoms for a couple of days, but has not had a sore throat or cough. His/her friend has convinced the student to present to the Emergency Department (ED) to be assessed for malaria.
TasksJson: ["Ask the patient about travel in the past two weeks, and ask about mosquito exposure.","Find out about the symptoms (e.g., temperature, headaches, joint aches, rash, etc.).","Discuss possible diagnoses (e.g., malaria, dengue fever, etc.) but explain that it is probably a non-specific viral disease.","Reassure the patient that there is no need for admission to the ED but suggest some basic blood tests in the ED and follow-up with the patient\u0027s general practitioner (GP).","Persuade the patient to stay in the ED now for blood tests."]

ScenarioTitle: This 34-year-old patient is attending because his/her spouse has noticed a small dark skin lesion on the patient's lower back.
Background: This 34-year-old patient is attending because his/her spouse has noticed a small dark skin lesion on the patient's lower back. The patient is concerned that this represents a skin cancer, and requests your opinion on management. You diagnose a benign, simple pigmented nevus that has probably been present for many years.
TasksJson: ["Explain the diagnosis (most likely birthmark, mole, etc.) and reassure the patient.","Explain the treatment: excising the lesion under local anesthetic (an excisional biopsy) and using histopathological examination (examination under microscope) to determine the nature of the lesion (a simple process: can be done in your rooms with minimal risk; results available in a few days).","Explain the procedure if the lesion is malignant: urgent referral to a surgeon for a wider excision of the lesion and probably adjuvant therapy (chemo- or radiotherapy). Based on the clinical appearance of the lesion, there is no need for urgent admission for a large-scale procedure immediately."]

ScenarioTitle: You have just examined the patient, an 18-year-old basketball player who has been brought to your surgery today by the team coach because of
Background: You have just examined the patient, an 18-year-old basketball player who has been brought to your surgery today by the team coach because of severe left knee pain. You diagnose a meniscus tear (torn cartilage).
TasksJson: ["Take a brief history from the patient.","Explain the likely diagnosis of a meniscus tear in a way that he/she will understand.","Discuss immediate treatment (e.g., RICER regime \u2013 Rest, Ice, Compress, Elevation and Referral to physiotherapist).","Explain why pain medication is not effective on its own.","Explain why you are referring the patient to a physiotherapist (e.g., appropriate exercise plan, recovery strategy, specific treatments, etc.).","Advise why he/she must not play sport until the pain has resolved and explain what the consequences of ignoring this advice could be."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 49-year-old accountant, married with two children.
Background: Your patient is a 49-year-old accountant, married with two children. He/she presented three weeks ago with a one-month history of rectal bleeding, diarrhoea and 2kg weight loss. You requested a colonoscopy and today the patient is returning for the results. Unfortunately, the patient has a tumour in the descending colon and the biopsy result confirms cancer.
TasksJson: ["Tell the patient the biopsy results (2cm tumour, confined to bowel wall) and recommend urgent referral to a surgeon.","Explain that management of the illness after surgery may include chemo/radiotherapy, depending on the spread of the tumour (but only with patient\u0027s consent).","Explain that a colostomy is unlikely as the tumour is confined to descending colon.","Encourage the patient to be optimistic about surgery (e.g., success rates are usually high; biopsy indicates that tumour is limited to bowel wall)."]

ScenarioTitle: Your 49-year-old patient has been recently diagnosed with Hashimoto's thyroiditis, an autoimmune disease which destroys the thyroid gland an
Background: Your 49-year-old patient has been recently diagnosed with Hashimoto's thyroiditis, an autoimmune disease which destroys the thyroid gland and leads to a range of symptoms (including weight gain, depression, fatigue and irregular heart rhythms). The endocrinologist has advised your patient to inform his/her two adult children, as the condition is hereditary. Your patient has some concerns and seeks your advice.
TasksJson: ["Reassure the patient that his/her medical records remain confidential. As the condition is neither life-threatening nor preventable, disclosure is not urgent or enforceable.","Encourage disclosure and give reasons (e.g., careful lifestyle management might prevent early onset; disclosure ensures accurate diagnosis at onset of illness).","Reassure the patient \u2013 you cannot advise on insurance policies but think that there are many benefits to be gained from disclosure.","Try to convince the patient to consider disclosure and offer referral to a genetic counsellor."]

ScenarioTitle: This 29-year-old lawyer has been experiencing heart palpitations.
Background: This 29-year-old lawyer has been experiencing heart palpitations. The patient is extremely busy, eats fast food very often and consumes large amounts of coffee. Both his/her physical examination and ECG are normal.
TasksJson: ["Ask the patient about his/her heart palpitations.","Suggest that the patient\u0027s symptoms could be caused by stress and anxiety.","Empathise with the patient\u0027s situation but inform him/her that the symptoms are not due to coronary problems (e.g., ECG and physical exam normal, etc.).","Give suggestions to help the patient manage the heart palpitations (e.g., stress management, reduction in caffeine intake, etc.). Include a healthier diet as a suggestion.","Recommend ways of eating healthier (e.g., making healthier choices in restaurant, etc.) and explain that these are important for long-term health."]

ScenarioTitle: You see an 86-year-old patient who has limited mobility. He/she uses a walking frame, and attends regular chair exercise classes.
Background: You see an 86-year-old patient who has limited mobility. He/she uses a walking frame, and attends regular chair exercise classes. He/she has come to see you about discomfort in his/her lower back. You suspect mild back strain.
TasksJson: ["Find out reason for patient\u0027s visit.","Find out more details about problem (exact location, any pain, etc.). Explore any possible causes (injury, exercise, etc.).","Give possible diagnosis of mild back strain (over-stretching of muscles/ligaments: not cause for concern, etc.). Advise on next steps (e.g., physical examination to confirm diagnosis, etc.). Recommend one week off exercise classes (e.g., not exercising when in pain, not ignoring pain, etc.).","Stress importance of rest from exercise (e.g., prevention of further injury/strain, time to recover, etc.). Make further recommendations (e.g., heat pack, paracetamol/acetaminophen, etc.).","Emphasise benefits of exercise classes (e.g., improved posture, maintaining muscle strength, boosting energy/mood, social interaction, etc.). Advise against overdoing exercise (e.g., awareness of own limits, etc.). Establish patient\u0027s consent for physical examination."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 54-year-old widow/er with advancing motor neurone disease.
Background: Your patient is a 54-year-old widow/er with advancing motor neurone disease. The son wants to become your patient's enduring medical power of attorney (MPOA), someone who makes medical treatment decisions for a person should that person lose the capacity to make those decisions. Your patient is not close to his/her son, feels pressure to appoint him as MPOA, and wants advice.
TasksJson: ["Explain that it is not necessary to appoint a MPOA and he/she can appoint someone other than his/her son.","Provide reassurance \u2013 no one can appoint themselves as MPOA for another person. The patient must have the capacity to understand the implications and consequences of appointing MPOA (otherwise it is not legally valid).","Reassure the patient that he/she will be supported during illness (MPOA cannot arrange euthanasia or refuse palliative care).","Offer to prepare an advance care plan for the patient so he/she can document his/her end of life choices; ensure he/she has a will."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 58 year old company accountant with a demanding job.
Background: Your patient is a 58 year old company accountant with a demanding job. He/she is overweight and doesn't exercise regularly. Recently, your patient has been feeling unusually tired, has lost a few kilograms and his/her vision is a bit blurry. The patient feels overworked and thinks the long hours on the computer are causing eye strain and he/she needs reading glasses. Your patient's spouse urged him/her to see the doctor about the eye issues.
TasksJson: ["Explain that the blurred vision might be caused by diabetes.","Recommend tests for diabetes (including on-the-spot random blood glucose finger prick). Reassure the patient that the tests are straightforward.","Explain why you think it might be diabetes (positive risk factors: history of being overweight, inactive, recent onset of lethargy, blurred vision and weight loss).","Recommend a referral to an ophthalmologist. Try to convince the patient to undergo testing for diabetes."]

ScenarioTitle: You are a general practitioner. The patient is a 24-year-old teacher who has come to your surgery today complaining of severe one-sided head
Background: You are a general practitioner. The patient is a 24-year-old teacher who has come to your surgery today complaining of severe one-sided headaches. These headaches lead to nausea and have been occurring over the last three months. The patient reports a family history of severe headaches. A trigger seems to be red wine consumption, suggesting migraine.
TasksJson: ["Take a history of the complaint and explain the need for a neurological examination (to check for signs of neurological disease).","Reassure the patient and discuss why you believe migraine is the likely cause.","Talk about the treatment options for migraine \u2013 preventative as well as abortive, and deal with the patient\u0027s questions about medication (barbiturates are habit-forming and not used much nowadays)."]

ScenarioTitle: This 27-year-old patient is presenting with a painful, red and swollen 2cm cut on his/her upper left thigh.
Background: This 27-year-old patient is presenting with a painful, red and swollen 2cm cut on his/her upper left thigh. Three days ago, the patient fell and cut his/her thigh on a piece of metal. You have examined the cut and determined that it is infected and will require treatment.
TasksJson: ["Ask if the patient has taken anything for the wound, applied any medications to the area, and if the patient has been immunised against tetanus.","Explain that the cut seems to be infected and will require treatment (e.g., antibiotics, etc.).","Convince the patient that it is necessary to clean the wound and give reasons why (e.g., foreign bodies present, etc.).","Suggest another tetanus injection as the last dose was a long time ago.","Explain that you want to see the patient tomorrow to review the wound, and that if it continues to deteriorate, surgical debridement (e.g., removal of unhealthy tissue, etc.) might be necessary."]

ScenarioTitle: You are speaking to a 50-year-old who dropped a 20kg weight on his/her left foot this morning when he/she was lifting weights at the gymnasi
Background: You are speaking to a 50-year-old who dropped a 20kg weight on his/her left foot this morning when he/she was lifting weights at the gymnasium. He/she has come to the Emergency Department to have the foot treated and to get a cast as he/she thinks it is broken. On examination you confirm that only the little toe is broken.
TasksJson: ["Explain that the little toe is broken but should heal by itself with proper care (e.g., elevation, ice, rest, avoid putting weight on it, etc.).","Explain that a cast will not help the toe to heal and will cause difficulties with mobility.","Stress that fitting a cast will cause atrophy of other muscles in the leg making rehabilitation more difficult.","Persuade the patient that a splint on the toe would be more beneficial than a cast.","Recommend paracetamol for pain relief and wearing sturdy shoes until the toe heals (in about 6 weeks)."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 26-year-old student who returned from an overseas vacation recently.
Background: Your patient is a 26-year-old student who returned from an overseas vacation recently. The patient has felt as though he/she has had flu symptoms for a couple of days, but has not had a sore throat or cough. His/her friend has convinced the student to present to the Emergency Department (ED) to be assessed for malaria.
TasksJson: ["Ask the patient about travel in the past two weeks, and ask about mosquito exposure.","Find out about the symptoms (e.g., temperature, headaches, joint aches, rash, etc.).","Discuss possible diagnoses (e.g., malaria, dengue fever, etc.) but explain that it is probably a non-specific viral disease.","Reassure the patient that there is no need for admission to the ED but suggest some basic blood tests in the ED and follow-up with the patient\u0027s general practitioner (GP).","Persuade the patient to stay in the ED now for blood tests."]

ScenarioTitle: This 55-year-old unmarried clerk is returning to your surgery today for a follow-up visit after a two-month period of hypertension for which
Background: This 55-year-old unmarried clerk is returning to your surgery today for a follow-up visit after a two-month period of hypertension for which he/she was briefly hospitalised. The patient is moderately overweight and inactive. His/her last two BP readings (taken by a community nurse) were 150/102 and 162/108. A prescription for atenolol (to treat hypertension) was issued one month ago. Today, on examination, you find that the patient’s BP reading is 160/100.
TasksJson: ["Explain your concern about the patient\u2019s condition and find out if he/she has been following the treatment plan.","Talk over any concerns and encourage the patient to continue with the prescribed medication.","Advise the patient of the dangers of not treating the hypertension.","Convince the patient to start the medication immediately."]

ScenarioTitle: A 33-year-old patient presents complaining of enlarged cervical and axillary lymph nodes that become worse after drinking alcohol.
Background: A 33-year-old patient presents complaining of enlarged cervical and axillary lymph nodes that become worse after drinking alcohol. The patient has looked on the internet and is convinced it is Hodgkin's lymphoma. He/she is very upset and anxious. On examination, you find no evidence of enlarged spleen or liver, but there is lymphadenopathy in the cervical nodes. You are unable to feel any axillary nodes or supraclavicular nodes.
TasksJson: ["Question the patient about associated symptoms (e.g., fatigue, weight loss, night sweats) and family history.","Reassure the patient that it is unlikely to be serious and explain your findings to him/her (lymphadenopathy in cervical nodes).","Explain what lymphadenopathy is (e.g., swelling of lymph nodes) and what might cause it (e.g., infection, etc.).","Suggest blood tests to investigate possible causes (e.g., complete blood count to show infection, etc.).","Agree to consider referring him/her for specialist opinion after the test results are returned."]

ScenarioTitle: This 31-year-old, otherwise healthy patient has been experiencing stomach cramps, nausea, diarrhoea and dizziness for two weeks since swimmi
Background: This 31-year-old, otherwise healthy patient has been experiencing stomach cramps, nausea, diarrhoea and dizziness for two weeks since swimming in a water hole (a natural hole where water collects) on a hiking trip. He/she originally thought it was the flu, but is now seeking your advice as the symptoms are persisting.
TasksJson: ["Question the patient to determine if he/she swallowed any contaminated water.","Explain what \u0027contaminants\u0027 in contaminated water are (e.g., micro-organisms from animal or human waste, etc.).","Recommend tests to confirm the cause (e.g., stool sample microscopy, culture and sensitivity, parasites, ova and cysts, test for Norovirus, etc.).","Recommend symptomatic treatment for now (e.g., antiemetics, etc.) and waiting until the test results come back for specific treatment.","Advise against anti-diarrhoeal agents until tests confirm there is no infective (bacterial or viral) cause for the diarrhoea.","Highlight the need to maintain adequate hydration."]

ScenarioTitle: Your 50-year-old patient is an office worker who broke his/her right arm during a fall six weeks ago.
Background: Your 50-year-old patient is an office worker who broke his/her right arm during a fall six weeks ago. The fibreglass cast was due to be removed this week but X-rays reveal that the break is not yet healed. The patient has a medical history of asthma and has been on corticosteroids for three months. You suspect osteoporosis.
TasksJson: ["Ask about the patient\u0027s family history of osteoporosis and other risk factors (e.g., low vitamin D intake, low calcium intake, etc.).","Tell the patient you suspect he/she may have osteoporosis.","Explain osteoporosis (e.g., condition where bones become less dense and more likely to break, etc.).","Refer the patient for bone mineral density testing at the local hospital.","Explain the Dual Energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DEXA) method of bone testing (e.g., X-ray beams of different energy, detects bone and soft tissue separately, safe and painless, usually takes a few minutes, etc.).","Reassure the patient that there are no complications with DEXA testing aside from a small radiation dose."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a fit, active 25-year-old. Recently, the patient has had trouble with his/her right knee especially after running and playin
Background: Your patient is a fit, active 25-year-old. Recently, the patient has had trouble with his/her right knee especially after running and playing sport. You suspect patellofemoral pain syndrome (kneecap pain). He/she has come to seek your advice.
TasksJson: ["Find out the patient\u0027s exercise routine (e.g., sport, gym, running, etc.).","Discuss the possibility that the patient has patellofemoral pain syndrome (e.g., muscle imbalance/misalignment, often caused by injury or high impact exercise, etc.).","Highlight that the condition should improve with physiotherapy. Stress the need for a temporary reduction in high-impact exercise.","Encourage the patient to change to lower impact exercise (e.g., bike riding, rowing machines, swimming, etc.) until after he/she has consulted the physiotherapist."]

ScenarioTitle: This 55-year-old unmarried clerk is returning to your surgery today for a follow-up visit after a two-month period of hypertension for which
Background: This 55-year-old unmarried clerk is returning to your surgery today for a follow-up visit after a two-month period of hypertension for which he/she was briefly hospitalised. The patient is moderately overweight and inactive. His/her last two BP readings (taken by a community nurse) were 150/102 and 162/108. A prescription for atenolol (to treat hypertension) was issued one month ago. Today, on examination, you find that the patient's BP reading is 160/100.
TasksJson: ["Explain your concern about the patient\u0027s condition and find out if he/she has been following the treatment plan.","Talk over any concerns and encourage the patient to continue with the prescribed medication.","Advise the patient of the dangers of not treating the hypertension.","Convince the patient to start the medication immediately."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a recently retired 65-year-old person with an active lifestyle.
Background: Your patient is a recently retired 65-year-old person with an active lifestyle. He/she usually sleeps well overnight. Increasingly, the patient is waking with cramps in the calves and is now disturbing his/her spouse. The patient is seeking your advice.
TasksJson: ["Find out why the patient has come to see you now.","Ask the patient about general health and wellbeing (e.g., exercise, diet, etc.).","Explain that significant mineral deficiencies are not a common cause in otherwise healthy people and it is more likely that overexertion may contribute to cramping (e.g., excessive exercise, muscle injury/fatigue, etc.).","Provide some recommendations for treatment (e.g., ice pack, regular stretching, massage, etc.).","Encourage the patient to visit a physiotherapist and to return for review in the future if necessary."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is 50 years old and has come to enquire about a Boostrix vaccine (combined diphtheria, tetanus and acellular pertussis (dTpa) v
Background: Your patient is 50 years old and has come to enquire about a Boostrix vaccine (combined diphtheria, tetanus and acellular pertussis (dTpa) vaccine). The patient's daughter is going to have a baby and she is encouraging the patient to get the vaccine, as she has heard that some illnesses can be fatal for infants. The patient's daughter believes that if the patient is vaccinated, it will help protect the baby from these illnesses. The patient has come to discuss the matter with you.
TasksJson: ["Ask the patient about his/her reason for presenting today.","Explain what a Boostrix vaccine consists of (e.g., diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough), and that it is recommended for adults in close contact with newborns.","Persuade the patient to have the injection and give reasons why whooping cough may be fatal to an infant (e.g., severe relentless coughing, hypoxic encephalopathy, may lead to brain damage and even death, etc.).","Explain that the risks of diphtheria and tetanus are low but the vaccine is a three-in-one injection.","Suggest that the patient return next week for the vaccine."]

Background: This 31-year-old, otherwise healthy patient has been experiencing stomach cramps, nausea, diarrhoea and dizziness for two weeks since swimming in a water hole (a natural hole where water collects) on a hiking trip. He/she originally thought it was the flu, but is now seeking your advice as the symptoms are persisting.
TasksJson: ["Question the patient to determine if he/she swallowed any contaminated water.","Explain what \u0027contaminants\u0027 in contaminated water are (e.g., micro-organisms from animal or human waste, etc.).","Recommend tests to confirm the cause (e.g., stool sample microscopy, culture and sensitivity, parasites, ova and cysts, test for Norovirus, etc.).","Recommend symptomatic treatment for now (e.g., antiemetics, etc.) and waiting until the test results come back for specific treatment.","Advise against anti-diarrhoeal agents until tests confirm there is no infective (bacterial or viral) cause for the diarrhoea.","Highlight the need to maintain adequate hydration."]

ScenarioTitle: This patient has recently been diagnosed with emphysema of which there is a family history.
Background: This patient has recently been diagnosed with emphysema of which there is a family history. He/she feels guilty for getting it, due to having smoked for 25 years. He/she has come for more information about the condition, and to find out what can be done to improve his/her quality of life, and possibly extend life expectancy.
TasksJson: ["Explain the condition to the patient \u2013 \u0027air-trapping\u0027 (i.e., air/gas trapped in the lungs due to difficulty exhaling completely).","Prescribe appropriate drugs \u2013 bronchodilators and/or steroid inhalers.","Recommend chest physiotherapy and outline ways in which this can help (e.g., breathing techniques to improve lung function and to increase tolerance to physical activity).","Answer questions about the surgical option (e.g., lung reduction) and the benefits it can offer.","Explain the narrow window of opportunity for surgery (e.g., age, condition, etc.).","Answer questions about prevention of secondary infections (e.g., stop smoking immediately, antibiotics, etc.).","Try to allay the patient\u0027s feelings of guilt."]

ScenarioTitle: A parent presented two hours ago at the Emergency Department (ED) with his/her four-year-old son.
Setting: Emergency Department of a Large Metropolitan Hospital
Background: A parent presented two hours ago at the Emergency Department (ED) with his/her four-year-old son. The boy has a 36-hour history of recurrent vomiting and stomach pain. On presentation, the boy's vomit consisted of clear slightly bile-stained fluid, with no blood. He felt thirsty but was unable to keep anything down. You suspect viral gastroenteritis. He was given oral re-hydration fluids and observed for two hours and now you tell the parent that it is safe to discharge him. The parent becomes anxious.
TasksJson: ["Respond to the parent\u0027s questions. Explain viral gastroenteritis (e.g., an irritation of stomach or intestines due to infection with a virus, etc.).","Explain that oral re-hydration therapy is usually effective without the need for hospitalisation.","Convince the parent that it is safe to take his/her son home but to seek medical advice if he shows signs of severe dehydration (e.g., rapid heartbeat and breathing, weak pulse, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 39-year-old factory worker whose boss has ordered all workers to have the flu vaccination.
Background: Your patient is a 39-year-old factory worker whose boss has ordered all workers to have the flu vaccination. Your patient is anxious about having the flu vaccination, as his/her uncle had a bad reaction to the vaccine five years ago. However, he/she has recently applied for promotion and so feels under pressure to satisfy the boss. He/she seeks your advice.
TasksJson: ["Explain that anyone can have the vaccine but it is strongly recommended in at-risk populations (young children, pregnant women, elderly, reduced immunity, healthcare workers). Most \u2018flu-like\u2019 illnesses are not influenza and immunised workers will still get coughs/colds.","Explain that the vaccine is relatively safe, compared with complications of flu (e.g., pneumonia, inflammation of brain/heart, etc.).","Reassure the patient that the boss cannot access medical records without the patient\u2019s consent.","Convince the patient that he/she alone must decide on whether or not to have the flu vaccination."]

ScenarioTitle: This 41-year-old patient has been experiencing pain and swelling in the right shoulder.
Background: This 41-year-old patient has been experiencing pain and swelling in the right shoulder. He/she usually plays cricket in his/her spare time, which involves swinging a bat and throwing a ball. You have examined the shoulder and diagnosed bursitis (small fluid-filled sacs usually between the muscles, tendons or bones).
TasksJson: ["Ask when the patient first began experiencing the pain and if the patient injured the shoulder.","Explain why it is unlikely the patient injured the shoulder while playing (e.g., would have felt pain during game, etc.).","Explain your diagnosis and what could have caused the bursitis (e.g., overuse, repeated pressure, etc.).","Persuade the patient to rest the shoulder and not to resume playing cricket until the swelling has gone down.","Suggest other ways to help manage the condition in the long-term (e.g., physiotherapy, joint protection techniques, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is 25 years old. His/her friend was recently diagnosed with a melanoma (skin cancer).
Background: Your patient is 25 years old. His/her friend was recently diagnosed with a melanoma (skin cancer). The patient is concerned that he/she might also be at risk of developing skin cancer, especially since he/she spent a lot of time on the beach during childhood and has been sunburnt on numerous occasions. The patient is extremely anxious and believes that the best way to avoid getting skin cancer is to have all his/her moles removed.
TasksJson: ["Reassure the patient that excising (surgically removing) moles is not necessary as skin cancer is usually preventable (e.g., mostly treatable if detected early; benign moles often arise in the 3rd and 4th decades of life, etc.).","Explain what changes to look for on skin spots (e.g., asymmetry, irregular border, different colouring, increasing diameter, change in shape/size, etc.).","Encourage prevention (e.g., regular skin checks, protect against sun damage, wear sun-cream, hat, protective clothing, etc.).","Offer to take photos and review in six months."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 39-year-old factory worker whose boss has ordered all workers to have the flu vaccination.
Background: Your patient is a 39-year-old factory worker whose boss has ordered all workers to have the flu vaccination. Your patient is anxious about having the flu vaccination, as his/her uncle had a bad reaction to the vaccine five years ago. However, he/she has recently applied for promotion and so feels under pressure to satisfy the boss. He/she seeks your advice.
TasksJson: ["Explain that anyone can have the vaccine but it is strongly recommended in at-risk populations (young children, pregnant women, elderly, reduced immunity, healthcare workers). Most \u2018flu-like\u2019 illnesses are not influenza and immunised workers will still get coughs/colds.","Explain that the vaccine is relatively safe, compared with complications of flu (e.g., pneumonia, inflammation of brain/heart, etc.).","Reassure the patient that the boss cannot access medical records without the patient\u2019s consent.","Convince the patient that he/she alone must decide on whether or not to have the flu vaccination."]

ScenarioTitle: The parent of a 3-year-old girl is seeking advice and a diagnosis (prior to the receipt of full test results) following the emergency admiss
Setting: Intensive Care Unit at Children's Hospital
Background: The parent of a 3-year-old girl is seeking advice and a diagnosis (prior to the receipt of full test results) following the emergency admission of his/her daughter yesterday. She was suffering from anaphylactic shock, almost certainly as a result of a food allergy. She is currently recovering after the subcutaneous administration of adrenaline. The parent appears calm.
TasksJson:
["Be sympathetic and reassuring.","Include the following information in your response to his/her questions:
- symptoms could have been caused by food/drink at party.
- confirmation of allergen to be done by administration of diagnostic tests.
- explanation of allergy: i.e., immune response (non-toxic substance treated as toxic by immune system), sometimes life-threatening.
- outlook: many children outgrow allergies.
- future prevention: avoid allergen (when identified); inform supervising adults of problem/causes/dangers.
- treatment of possible future episodes: adrenaline (using EpiPen autoinjector), immediate medical attention."]

ScenarioTitle: You are talking to a parent of a six-year-old boy who has had a sore throat and fever for two days.
Background: You are talking to a parent of a six-year-old boy who has had a sore throat and fever for two days. The parent noticed blood in the boy's urine this morning. The boy looks unwell and has a temperature of 38.5°C. His throat is swollen and red and there is exudate on the tonsils. A full ward test confirms blood in the urine. You diagnose bacterial tonsillitis with kidney involvement (poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis).
TasksJson: ["Explain to the parent the results of the urine test and the diagnosis.","Explain that the child requires further investigation and an urgent appointment with a paediatrician.","Explain that you would like to start a course of antibiotics (penicillin).","Address the parent\u0027s concerns about the use of antibiotics for a \u0027simple\u0027 throat infection by explaining the connection between the infection and the blood in the urine (e.g., the body produces extra antibodies to fight the infection, and these settle in the kidneys causing inflammation, etc.).","Answer the parent\u0027s questions about the next steps in the treatment of his/her son (e.g., refer to a paediatrician to monitor urine and blood pressure and make sure recovery is complete, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: You are working as a surgical resident in this hospital. You have been called to talk to a 45-year-old patient who is awaiting surgery for a
Background: You are working as a surgical resident in this hospital. You have been called to talk to a 45-year-old patient who is awaiting surgery for a large benign lipoma on his/her back. You note that the patient has already been booked into the outpatient clinic in two weeks for review of the wound and histopathology.
TasksJson: ["Reassure the patient that the risk of cancer is extremely low.","Explain that the lump will be examined under the microscope and the patient will normally get the results at the two-week review in the clinic. The wound will also be checked then.","Explain that there will be a scar as it is a large lesion but it will fade with time. Keeping the area dressed with steristrips for a month can help to minimise this. The surgeon will discuss this further with the patient.","Reassure the patient about removal of the lump and the unlikelihood of recurrence."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a recently retired 65-year-old person with an active lifestyle.
Background: Your patient is a recently retired 65-year-old person with an active lifestyle. He/she usually sleeps well overnight. Increasingly, the patient is waking with cramps in the calves and is now disturbing his/her spouse. The patient is seeking your advice.
TasksJson: ["Find out why the patient has come to see you now.","Ask the patient about general health and wellbeing (e.g., exercise, diet, etc.).","Explain that significant mineral deficiencies are not a common cause in otherwise healthy people and it is more likely that overexertion may contribute to cramping (e.g., excessive exercise, muscle injury/fatigue, etc.).","Provide some recommendations for treatment (e.g., ice pack, regular stretching, massage, etc.).","Encourage the patient to visit a physiotherapist and to return for review in the future if necessary."]

ScenarioTitle: A parent has brought in his/her nine-year-old daughter who underwent a tonsillectomy a week ago.
Background: A parent has brought in his/her nine-year-old daughter who underwent a tonsillectomy a week ago. The daughter has been using oxycodone quite liberally for post-operative pain, and is now suffering severe constipation. The child has no history of severe constipation and you have already examined the child.
TasksJson: ["Explain the link between the oxycodone and the daughter\u0027s symptoms.","Outline effective measures for resolving the constipation and recommend alternative pain relief.","Discuss whether the parent should avoid giving oxycodone to his/her daughter in the future (e.g., side effects are common but usually mild and short-lived, etc.).","Persuade the parent to be less liberal with the pain medication (e.g., tonsillectomy pain usually improves after first few days, etc.).","Answer questions about the benefits of ice-cream (e.g., eating normally helps the throat to heal, etc.) and salt water gargles (e.g., can relieve a sore throat, important not to swallow, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient has come to see you about his/her 16-year-old son whom he/she suspects is taking illegal drugs.
Background: Your patient has come to see you about his/her 16-year-old son whom he/she suspects is taking illegal drugs. The boy is not present.
TasksJson: ["Ask questions to establish why the parent thinks that his/her son is taking drugs.","Find out more about the boy (his lifestyle, friendship group, studies, etc.).","Find out what your patient would like you to do. Ask whether it would be possible for the boy to come to see you in person.","Suggest referring the boy to an adolescent psychologist for assessment and appropriate treatment.","Explain to the parent some of the possible effects of marijuana (e.g., can affect alertness, concentration, coordination, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: A middle-aged patient has come in complaining of a bitter taste in his/her mouth, which is worse on waking and accompanied by a burning sens
Background: A middle-aged patient has come in complaining of a bitter taste in his/her mouth, which is worse on waking and accompanied by a burning sensation in the back of the throat. He/she is overweight, and you notice a slight cough when he/she speaks. You diagnose GORD (gastro-oesophageal reflux disease).
TasksJson: ["Check if the patient has difficulty swallowing.","Tell the patient your diagnosis (GORD) and explain the causes (e.g., alcohol use, being overweight, smoking, bad posture).","Outline dietary and lifestyle measures that can help in controlling it (e.g., weight management - foods to avoid; meals - little and often and not within three hours of bed; lifestyle - smoking, alcohol, elevation of head of bed, avoidance of exercise straight after meal).","Advise on the treatment strategy: ranitidine (H2 antagonist) then review.","Reassure the patient. You do not feel a referral for an endoscopy is warranted at this stage. It may be worthwhile later if there is limited response to ranitidine."]

ScenarioTitle: An elderly patient presented several months ago with herpes zoster (shingles) on the right temporal region of the face.
Background: An elderly patient presented several months ago with herpes zoster (shingles) on the right temporal region of the face. He/she is now complaining of symptoms of postherpetic neuralgia (the nerve pain that often lingers after a shingles rash goes away).
TasksJson: ["Explain the cause of the symptoms to the patient (pain in the nerves).","Recommend analgesia as a first line of treatment (paracetamol or codeine). Give capsaicin cream for topical application and explain the sensation it might cause. (e.g., a slight stinging sensation or coughing and sneezing, etc.).","Mention anticonvulsant drugs (gabapentin or pregabalin) may be used if necessary.","Answer questions about excision of the affected area and reassure him/her that surgery is not indicated.","Explain that non-pharmacological approaches may help (e.g., relaxation, meditation, psychologist, chronic pain clinic, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 42-year-old financial adviser. He/she has a stressful job and frequently travels overseas on business.
Background: Your patient is a 42-year-old financial adviser. He/she has a stressful job and frequently travels overseas on business. A few months ago, a work colleague suggested that he/she take sleeping pills to help regulate sleep and ease anxiety. The patient came to see you and you prescribed a benzodiazepine. The patient has now run out of pills and so today he/she has come to request another prescription.
TasksJson: ["Ask the patient how often he/she takes the sleeping pills.","Explain to the patient that long term nightly use of any sleeping pill is not recommended (use of pills does not cure sleep problem; risk of drug dependency).","Tactfully refuse to prescribe another prescription.","Convince the patient to try non-medical interventions - e.g., regular exercise, control workload (learn to say \u0027no\u0027), reduce alcohol/caffeine, etc.","Caution against stopping the pills suddenly (risk of withdrawal symptoms) - gradually decrease the dose and consider other strategies for coping with his/her anxiety."]

ScenarioTitle: You have just examined the patient, an 18-year-old basketball player who has been brought to your surgery today by the team coach because of
Background: You have just examined the patient, an 18-year-old basketball player who has been brought to your surgery today by the team coach because of severe left knee pain. You diagnose a meniscus tear (torn cartilage).
TasksJson: ["Take a brief history from the patient.","Explain the likely diagnosis of a meniscus tear in a way that he/she will understand.","Discuss immediate treatment (e.g., RICER regime \u2013 Rest, Ice, Compress, Elevation and Referral to physiotherapist).","Explain why pain medication is not effective on its own.","Explain why you are referring the patient to a physiotherapist (e.g., appropriate exercise plan, recovery strategy, specific treatments, etc.).","Advise why he/she must not play sport until the pain has resolved and explain what the consequences of ignoring this advice could be."]

ScenarioTitle: You are a general practitioner. The patient is a 24-year-old teacher who has come to your surgery today complaining of severe one-sided head
Background: You are a general practitioner. The patient is a 24-year-old teacher who has come to your surgery today complaining of severe one-sided headaches. These headaches lead to nausea and have been occurring over the last three months. The patient reports a family history of severe headaches. A trigger seems to be red wine consumption, suggesting migraine.
TasksJson: ["Take a history of the complaint and explain the need for a neurological examination (to check for signs of neurological disease).","Reassure the patient and discuss why you believe migraine is the likely cause.","Talk about the treatment options for migraine \u2013 preventative as well as abortive, and deal with the patient\u2019s questions about medication (barbiturates are habit-forming and not used much nowadays)."]

ScenarioTitle: Your 62-year-old patient worries about his/her health. Three months ago, he/she commenced one tablet of standard aspirin daily, to keep the
Background: Your 62-year-old patient worries about his/her health. Three months ago, he/she commenced one tablet of standard aspirin daily, to keep the heart and blood healthy. The patient reports his/her blood pressure has never been better. However, lately the patient has been feeling lethargic and irritable. One month ago, he/she started having mild-moderate stomach pains. He/she presents today for a routine check-up and advice on the recent symptoms.
TasksJson: ["Recommend a trial period without aspirin as it may be causing gastric inflammation/ulceration. Suggest that the patient may also need anti-acid medication and proton-pump inhibitors.","Reassure the patient - blood pressure regulation relies on a number of factors (e.g., regular exercise, low sodium diet, etc.). Aspirin is not a necessary medication for this patient (nil cardiovascular disease/diabetes/renal disease).","Try to convince the patient that it is unlikely he/she has stomach cancer. A gastroscopy can be done to exclude cancer should his/her symptoms persist."]

ScenarioTitle: Your 50-year-old patient is concerned about his/her health. Cardiovascular illness runs in the family.
Background: Your 50-year-old patient is concerned about his/her health. Cardiovascular illness runs in the family. The patient's 61-year-old sister recently had a heart attack. The patient's medical check-up confirms that he/she has moderately elevated cholesterol and blood pressure. The sister's recent heart attack concerns the patient, who is desperate to avoid a similar event. He/she seeks your advice on how to avoid having a heart attack.
TasksJson: ["Find out about the patient\u0027s concerns.","Strongly recommend that the patient commence medication (e.g., beta-blockers) to reduce the risk of cardiac disease and death.","Reassure the patient about identifying and managing side effects (e.g., the patient has no contraindication for beta-blockers; common side effects can usually be managed with dose adjustments or suitable alternative medication, etc.).","Convince the patient that while lifestyle management remains crucial, medication is necessary for reducing the risk of cardiac disease and death."]

ScenarioTitle: An elderly patient has come to you after an acute episode of diverticulitis.
Background: An elderly patient has come to you after an acute episode of diverticulitis. He/she had acute onset of pain in the left iliac fossa and rectal bleeding for which he/she was hospitalised. The hospital report sent to you indicated no perforation, abscesses, peritonitis or fistula. The patient is extremely anxious as he/she was not given any information about the condition on discharge.
TasksJson: ["Reassure the patient that the hospital report indicates no perforation, etc.","Explain to the patient that the condition could recur.","Stress the importance of dietary modification to avoid constipation. However, excessive use of aperients (purgatives) should be avoided.","Explain why the antibiotic treatment was prescribed (bacterial infection of the colon can cause diverticular disease).","Advise the patient to return if rectal bleeding or bad abdominal pain recurs; a surveillance colonoscopy might be the next step if bowel habit alters or bleeding returns."]

ScenarioTitle: A patient presents complaining of red itchy eyes. He/she has signs of pink eye (conjunctivitis).
Background: A patient presents complaining of red itchy eyes. He/she has signs of pink eye (conjunctivitis). You take a history - use of contact lenses, or any recent contact with chemicals. Your patient has had recent symptoms of a discharge and itchiness, so you suspect viral or allergic conjunctivitis. You question your patient further to confirm your diagnosis.
TasksJson: ["Ask how long the discharge has occurred for \u2013 is it clear or purulent?","Find out if the patient has had a cold recently.","Explain your diagnosis of conjunctivitis and the possible cause (e.g., viral infection).","Explain the appropriate treatment and the usual course of conjunctivitis (e.g., virus: antihistamines, warm/cool compresses, etc.).","Answer questions about the need for an allergy test and the likelihood of recurrence.","Reassure the patient that it should not affect his/her vision permanently.","Advise the patient not to share face washers/bed linen with others as the condition is contagious."]

ScenarioTitle: You are speaking to the son/daughter of a middle-aged, overweight man.
Background: You are speaking to the son/daughter of a middle-aged, overweight man. He/she is concerned about the father, who lives in the same house (the mother died two years ago). He/she is worried that when the father stops breathing at night, he may not restart breathing. Recently, the father appears withdrawn and not interested in family life with his children and grandchildren. You suspect sleep apnoea.
TasksJson: ["Explain sleep apnoea (breathing stops momentarily during sleep) to the son/daughter and that a sleep study will be needed to establish the diagnosis.","Establish that sedating medications are not taken at night and excess alcohol is not contributing.","Reassure the son/daughter that effective treatment for sleep apnoea is available (e.g. continuous positive airway pressure therapy, etc.).","Provide advice on how the family might support the father to manage sleep apnoea through lifestyle changes (e.g., diet and exercise to reduce weight, etc.)","Discuss possible depression, as a separate diagnosis or as a consequence of the sleep apnoea."]

ScenarioTitle: The patient is a five-year-old girl. She and her family are in Australia visiting friends.
Background: The patient is a five-year-old girl. She and her family are in Australia visiting friends. She has a small, superficial dog bite wound on the side of the face, near the hair line. You are speaking to her parent.
TasksJson: ["Calm the parent. Find out the circumstances of the bite and first aid given.","After examination, reassure the parent that the wound needs only cleaning and closure, and explain how you will do this.","Antibiotics are not necessary \u2013 low risk of infection (e.g., a recent wound, the face has an excellent blood supply, etc.).","Check on the child\u2019s tetanus immunisation status and explain whether a booster is needed (NOTE: Australia is free of rabies).","Advise the parent on care of the wound \u2013 recommend a review after 48 hours.","Advise on the need for constant supervision of children near dogs."]

Background: A three-year-old boy has been stung by a bee. TasksJson:
["Gently refuse to organise for the child to be admitted to hospital.","Reassure the parent (e.g., localised response; already half an hour after the sting and no signs of systemic illness – hives, wheezing, shortness of breath, faintness or weakness, etc.).","Convince the parent to observe the son at home. - ice to soothe pain and reduce swelling.
- clean the affected area to avoid infection.
- treat itching with over-the-counter antihistamine (e.g., Benadryl)."]

ScenarioTitle: Sharing a new diagnosis of Type 2 Diabetes
Background: Mr Bellamy attends to discuss recent blood-test results. His HbA1c is consistent with a new diagnosis of Type 2 Diabetes. ScenarioTitle: Discussing chest-pain investigation results
Background: Ms Kowalska presented six weeks ago with episodic exertional chest tightness. She has completed an exercise tolerance test and a CT coronary angiogram, both of which are reassuring with no significant coronary disease. ScenarioTitle: Declining an antibiotic request for a viral illness
Background: Mr Hartwell attends with a three-day history of sore throat, runny nose, low-grade fever and a productive cough. TasksJson: ["Find out what he is most worried about and what he is hoping for today.", "Share your clinical findings and explain why this looks like a viral illness.", "Explain why antibiotics will not help in this situation in plain, respectful language.", "Offer a clear plan for symptom relief and safety-netting.", "Negotiate a path he can accept without leaving frustrated."]

ScenarioTitle: Lifestyle counselling for newly identified hypertension
Background: Ms Chandran has had three elevated clinic blood-pressure readings and a 24-hour ambulatory monitor confirming Stage 1 hypertension. She has no other cardiovascular risk factors today. She is hoping to address this with lifestyle changes before starting medication. She works long hours in IT and reports high stress and disrupted sleep.
TasksJson: ["Confirm the diagnosis in plain language and check her understanding.", "Find out what changes she feels are realistic for her in the next three months.", "Discuss the highest-yield lifestyle changes for her in particular.", "Address her preference to avoid starting medication today.", "Agree a measurable plan and a clear review point."]

ScenarioTitle: Sharing a new diagnosis of colorectal cancer
Setting: Surgical outpatient clinic, dedicated quiet room
Background: Mrs Ward underwent a colonoscopy two weeks ago after iron-deficiency anaemia and a change in bowel habit. Biopsy results have confirmed adenocarcinoma of the sigmoid colon. TasksJson: ["Check what she is expecting and what support she has with her today.", "Share the diagnosis honestly, clearly, and without overload.", "Allow time for her reaction and respond to it.", "Outline the immediate next steps (staging, MDT, contact nurse) at a pace she can absorb.", "Close safely, ensuring she does not leave alone or unsupported."]

ScenarioTitle: Explaining comfort care to a relative at end of life

Background: Mr Lyons has metastatic pancreatic cancer and was transferred to your palliative unit yesterday. The medical team has stopped active treatment and moved him onto a comfort-care plan.
