ScenarioTitle: You are talking to a 35-year-old computer engineer who has been referred by his/ her doctor for advice on weight loss.
Background: You are talking to a 35-year-old computer engineer who has been referred by his/ her doctor for advice on weight loss. The patient has been experiencing breathlessness on exertion and has been advised by his/her GP to lose weight to improve his/her health status. The patient is overweight and has a BMI of 25.
TasksJson: ["Discuss the importance of losing weight (breathlessness may be caused by overweight).","Ask questions about the patient\u0027s general lifestyle including drinking and eating habits","Provide advice on increasing physical activity and eating a suitable diet (reducing alcohol intake, eating fruits and vegetables).","Advise the patient to come back for a review in four weeks\u0027 time."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 51-year-old university lecturer admitted for surgery to remove a benign tumour from the superficial lobe of the parotid (s
Background: Your patient is a 51-year-old university lecturer admitted for surgery to remove a benign tumour from the superficial lobe of the parotid (salivary) gland. He/she has been told that there is a risk of facial nerve damage and permanent facial muscle weakness. You are preparing the patient for surgery.
TasksJson: ["Give reason for seeing patient (preparation for surgery). Find out about any patient concerns.","Confirm possible risks of surgery (e.g., facial nerve damage, permanent facial muscle weakness, etc.). Reassure patient about facial deformity and weakness after surgery (e.g., muscle weakness: most likely temporary, usually minimal, etc.).","Describe possible post-surgery side effects (e.g., incisional/facial swelling, skin numbness, jaw stiffness, fatigue, etc.). Explain when to see doctor (e.g., if experiencing: fever, ear drainage, saliva drainage from wound, etc.).","Advise patient on aftercare/improving recovery (e.g., antibiotic ointment, sleeping on 2\u20133 pillows, use of tight parotid wrap: reduction in swelling, etc.). Give advice about returning to work/other activities (e.g., work: 10\u201314 days after surgery; exercise: 3\u20134 weeks; etc.). Find out any other questions/concerns.","Reassure patient about prognosis (e.g., good: tumour benign/superficial, etc.). Establish patient\u0027s consent to proceed with preparation for surgery."]

ScenarioTitle: The son/daughter of an eighty-year-old woman has come to ask for information about cholesterol.
Background: The son/daughter of an eighty-year-old woman has come to ask for information about cholesterol. He/she wants information about his/her mother's current cholesterol level and how best to reduce it.
TasksJson: ["Find out what the son/daughter already knows about cholesterol","Inform your visitor about what cholesterol is (fat-like material present in the blood and most tissues) and about types of cholesterol (high density lipoproteins (HDL) good, low density lipoproteins (LDL)-bad).","Tactfully explain that if the fatty deposits are lodged in the arteries, this can lead to heart disease or stroke.","Explain what the doctor meant by a fairly high level of cholesterol (i.e., elevated above 5.5 mmols/liter in the blood).","Advice your visitor about how his/her mother can best deal with her cholesterol (e.g., avoid saturated fats and eat more fiber, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 52-year-old bank employee who had a cyst removed from his/her right leg yesterday.
Background: Your patient is a 52-year-old bank employee who had a cyst removed from his/her right leg yesterday. The wound has been bleeding a small amount and is slightly painful. The patient appears anxious.
TasksJson: ["Find out how the patient is doing.","Confirm that there are slight complications (i.e. bleeding, fever, pain) which are not uncommon post-surgery.","Advise the patient to stay until their symptoms resolve.","Explain that management involves more than just painkillers (regular temperature checking, monitoring incision site, antibiotics for possible infection, etc.).","Continue to tell the patient that early discharge is not advised as a review by the surgeon is needed and the biopsy results are not available yet. Remind them that their sutures will be removed on day 3 or 4.","Strongly advise against driving at this stage and find out the patient\u0027s decision."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a busy 50-year-old waitress, recently diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes.
Background: Your patient is a busy 50-year-old waitress, recently diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes. The patient had a wedge resection 12 days ago and has post-operative staphylococcus aureus (staph infection, non-MRSA) on the right large toe. You are visiting the home to change the dressing whilst the patient is resting from work duties.
TasksJson: ["Find out about the patient\u2019s general daily habits after the operation. Did the patient rest adequately?","Highlight the fact that sometimes people get post operative infection but it is not really their fault.","Persuade your patient to rest and that the toe will heal with attendance to dressings, fresh air and daily exposure to the sun, antibiotics, etc.","Explain the risks of circulation problems for diabetics and sometimes greater risk of infection.","Supply a patient information brochure to the patient and agree to call again next week."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a four-year-old boy who has been given eight sutures (stitches) on his right arm after falling and cutting his arm.
Background: Your patient is a four-year-old boy who has been given eight sutures (stitches) on his right arm after falling and cutting his arm. He is now ready to be discharged. You are seeing the parent to give advice on aftercare. The child is not present for the discussion.
TasksJson: ["Confirm reason for seeing parent (advice on aftercare). Find out parent\u0027s feelings about child going home.","Give advice on wound care (e.g., keeping dry/covered, dressing in place until removal of sutures, etc.). Advise on bathing (e.g., after 48 hours, no immersion in water, careful drying, re-applying dressing, etc.). Recommend continued pain relief (e.g., every six hours, for 48 hours/until wound starts to heal, etc.).","Stress importance of pain relief (e.g., pain from large wound/trauma, number of sutures, etc.).","Make recommendations (e.g., until removal of sutures: plenty of rest/fluids, avoiding rough play, etc.). Give information about removal of sutures (e.g., nurse appointment at clinic, in ten days, etc.). Advise when medical attention necessary (e.g., high temperature, bleeding, lack of appetite, etc.). Find out any other concerns.","Reassure parent about scarring (e.g., initially only, usually fades completely with time, etc.). Advise opportunity for further discussion about scarring (e.g., during removal of sutures, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: You see a 48-year-old patient who is going to have a cholecystectomy (gall bladder removal) in three days.
Background: You see a 48-year-old patient who is going to have a cholecystectomy (gall bladder removal) in three days. The patient has asked to speak to you.
TasksJson: ["Find out reason for patient\u0027s request to see you.","Explore reasons for patient\u0027s nervousness (surgery, anaesthetics, etc.).","Reassure patient about general anaesthetic (e.g., routine, managed by specialist doctor or anaesthetist, no need to worry, etc.). Give information about gall bladder operation (e.g., common, usually done as keyhole surgery, short recovery time, etc.).","Emphasise reasons for operation (e.g., diagnosis of chronic cholecystitis, high likelihood of recurrence, etc.). Give information about gall bladder (e.g., for bile storage, not essential, liver production of bile sufficient for digestion, etc.).","Explain preoperative requirements (e.g., fasting from six hours before, removing piercings/nail varnish, showering before operation, etc.). Explain postoperative steps (e.g., likely same-day discharge, assistance getting home, etc.). Explore patient\u0027s post-surgery discharge plans (relative/friend to escort home and stay 24 hours, etc.).","Outline aftereffects of operation (e.g., effects of anaesthetic, pain at incision point, shoulder pain due to gas used to inflate abdomen, bloating, etc.). Find out any other questions/concerns."]

ScenarioTitle: You see a 28-year-old accountant, recently diagnosed with type 1 (insulin-dependent) diabetes.
Background: You see a 28-year-old accountant, recently diagnosed with type 1 (insulin-dependent) diabetes. He/she is very anxious about having to inject him/herself on a daily basis. The patient is attending the clinic today to find out more about the insulin injections.
TasksJson: ["Confirm reason for patient\u0027s visit (insulin injection information). Find out how patient is feeling about diabetes diagnosis.","Find out what patient knows about type 1 diabetes.","Give information about type 1 diabetes (e.g., not sugar problem, failure of body to produce insulin, excess sugar in blood, managed through insulin injections, etc.).","Reassure patient about injections (e.g., insulin pens usually painless, needles small/thin, becomes routine, etc.).","Advise patient on possible side effects of insulin therapy (e.g., initial weight gain, swelling of arms/legs, etc.). Stress benefits of insulin therapy (e.g., increased energy, better lifestyle flexibility, improved well-being, etc.).","Emphasise that insulin injections won\u0027t cure diabetes (e.g., only delay/prevent complications of diabetes: vision impairment, poor peripheral circulation, etc.). Offer to show patient how to do insulin injections."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 79-year-old who presented to emergency last night with chest pain, nausea and vomiting.
Background: Your patient is a 79-year-old who presented to emergency last night with chest pain, nausea and vomiting. An ECG and blood tests showed evidence of a mild myocardial infarction. The cardiologist recommended an angiogram to be performed but the patient feels anxious and unprepared. The attending cardiologist has asked you to explain the procedure and associated risks to the patient.
TasksJson: ["Ask the patient about his/her concerns","Briefly explain the angiogram procedure (X-rays taken to see the heart vessels in detail) and the procedure (Sedation given, catheter placed in wrist or groin and guided into the heart)","Reassure and explain that complications are rare (reaction to dye, stroke, cardiac arrest, death)","Explain that angiogram is the best way to know the condition of the arteries and to check for any blockages","Accept that the patient wants to seek another opinion before having the angiogram"]

ScenarioTitle: You are attending to a 52-year-old who works long hours in customer service.
Background: You are attending to a 52-year-old who works long hours in customer service. The patient complains of being tired and has been experiencing aching feet. Sometimes he/she has numbness and tingling, which is worse at night. The patient admits to being ‘paranoid’ as his/her uncle has Multiple Sclerosis and his/her aunt has Parkinson’s disease.
TasksJson: ["Explain that working long hours and stress may produce symptoms such as tiredness and poor memory.","Suggest initial steps to improve sore feet issues (e.g. comfortable shoes, orthopedic shoes; compression stockings, etc.).","Emphasise that you think the patient may be putting too much pressure on him/herself.","Explain that you will examine his/her feet for obvious signs of injury and suggest a visit to a podiatrist.","Advise the patient to arrange a medical appointment.","Highlight the importance of not self-diagnosing and thinking the worst."]

ScenarioTitle: You see a 50-year-old patient who has been catheterised (a small tube has been inserted into the bladder to empty it) to relieve urinary ret
Background: You see a 50-year-old patient who has been catheterised (a small tube has been inserted into the bladder to empty it) to relieve urinary retention following an operation. You have come to remove the catheter for a trial without catheter (TWOC).
TasksJson: ["Find out how patient is feeling (any improvement in pain/discomfort, etc.).","Explain need for removal of catheter (e.g., TWOC: trial without catheter; followed by bladder scan; etc.). Find out any questions/concerns.","Emphasise importance of removing catheter (e.g., restoring normal bladder function, etc.). Remind patient catheter is temporary measure (e.g., short-term relief, etc.).","Resist patient\u0027s request to speak to doctor (e.g., decision made by doctor, removal of catheter: common practice, etc.). Outline risks of leaving catheter in (e.g., infection, inflammation, bleeding, etc.). Reassure patient about pain (e.g., possibility of catheter reinsertion: if problems persist, etc.).","Explain preventative measures (e.g., prescription medication, avoidance of over-the-counter medication: associated with urinary retention, etc.). Establish patient\u0027s consent for removal of catheter."]

ScenarioTitle: You visit a 72-year-old patient who was discharged three days ago after having spent a month in hospital with sepsis.
Background: You visit a 72-year-old patient who was discharged three days ago after having spent a month in hospital with sepsis. You are visiting the patient to dress his/her wound.
TasksJson: ["Confirm reason for your visit (wound management following hospital stay with sepsis). Find out how patient has been since discharge (mobility, fatigue, appetite, etc.).","Stress importance of good nutrition (e.g., aiding recovery, building up strength, etc.). Find out about patient\u0027s food and fluid intake (amount, frequency, etc.).","Make suggestions for eating (e.g., little and often, preferred foods, nutritional high-calorie foods, supplemental nutrition drinks, etc.). Explore any other symptoms (any pain/fever, swelling in limbs, difficulty sleeping, etc.).","Remind patient about sepsis recovery (e.g., fatigue normal, slow/gradual process, etc.). Find out any other questions/concerns.","Reassure patient about his/her current condition (e.g., recovering as expected, no obvious cause for concern, etc.). Outline next steps (e.g., checking and redressing wound, checking vital signs, doctor\u0027s appointment: precaution, etc.). Establish patient\u0027s consent to have wound checked and redressed."]

ScenarioTitle: This 35-year-old patient was involved in a car accident earlier today and is now Suffering from a headache and whiplash (an injury to the ce
Background: This 35-year-old patient was involved in a car accident earlier today and is now Suffering from a headache and whiplash (an injury to the cervical spine). He/she is being kept in the hospital for observation but is expected to be discharged later in the day.
TasksJson: ["Find out what the patient thinks are the reasons why he/she is being kept in the hospital.","Advise the patient on the reason for taking and continuing to take medication and ways of managing the pain once he/she returns home (0.g., with heat/ice, analgesics, a collar, etc.).","Discuss the best care practices for after the patient leaves the hospital","Describe the benefits of consulting a physiotherapist about exercise and relaxation exercises to loosen up the joints.","Explain that you cannot be sure how long the patient will take to recover fully","Stress the importance of complying with the treatment and exercise program.","Stress the importance of seeking medical advice if there is any increased pain or discomfort, nausea, vomiting, or vision problems."]

ScenarioTitle: You are talking to the parent of 12-year-old Isabelle, who has just been admitted after a fall from a tree.
Background: You are talking to the parent of 12-year-old Isabelle, who has just been admitted after a fall from a tree. A skull fracture is suspected so the doctor has ordered a CT scan and X-rays. Her parent is demanding to go with her while the procedures are done, but hospital policy does not allow it.
TasksJson: ["Find out what happened to Isabelle.","Reassure the parent about the current situation (did the right thing bringing Isabelle to hospital, accidents happen, doctor is very experienced, etc.).","Explain that a skull fracture is suspected, and the importance of the CT scan and X-ray being undertaken quickly.","Explain why the parent needs to remain in the waiting room (dangers of radiation exposure, parent could slow down the process, etc.).","Convince the parent that a nurse will be by Isabelle\u2019s side during the procedures.","Advise that they will be called when the doctor gets the results."]

ScenarioTitle: You see the son/daughter and main carer of a 75-year-old woman.
Background: You see the son/daughter and main carer of a 75-year-old woman. His/her mother has dementia and has recently had a cholecystectomy (surgery to remove the gall bladder) and is now being discharged. You are discussing the aftercare that is required. His/her mother is not present.
TasksJson: ["Confirm reason for son/daughter\u0027s appointment (information about mother\u0027s aftercare post-discharge). Find out about mother\u0027s living arrangements.","Describe benefits of living with family (e.g., practical/emotional support, social interaction, etc.). Explore son/daughter\u0027s view of mother\u0027s recovery so far (physical strength, energy, mood, etc.).","Emphasise necessity of extended stays for some patients (e.g., age, slower recovery, etc.). Give details of mother\u0027s progress (e.g., no infection, improvement in appetite, minor discomfort, etc.).","Explain mother\u0027s wound care (e.g., cleaning daily, keeping covered, soluble stitches: disappear in 2\u20133 weeks, etc.). Outline medication (e.g., oral antibiotics for five days, pain relief as required, laxative twice daily unless stool is loose, etc.). Describe restrictions (e.g., no lifting, gentle exercise, small/frequent meals, etc.).","Reassure son/daughter about post-discharge information (e.g., in discharge pack, etc.). Outline further support available (e.g., community nurse, mother\u0027s doctor, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 79-year-old who has been on the waiting list for over a year for a cataract operation.
Background: Your patient is a 79-year-old who has been on the waiting list for over a year for a cataract operation. The surgery to the right eye has been completed this morning. You are checking the patient's recovery and vision.
TasksJson: ["Ask about the patient\u0027s sight after removing the eye patch.","Reassure patient about the normal recovery process (blurry, scratchy vision normal, improvement of vision usually 24-48 hours post-surgery). Confirm patient accepts your explanation of post-op symptoms.","Provide reassurance about the return of good eyesight in a couple of days.","Explain the importance of infection prevention (eye drops 4 times per day, avoidance of dusty areas, no eye rubbing, etc.). Confirm patient\u0027s ability to administer eye drops.","Offer to organise a nurse home visit for assistance with eyedrops application.","Explain signs of possible infection (eye discharge, pain, increased sensitivity to light, etc.) and the need for medical attention if this occurs."]

ScenarioTitle: You see a parent whose three-year-old daughter gets severe motion sickness when she is travelling in a car.
Background: You see a parent whose three-year-old daughter gets severe motion sickness when she is travelling in a car. The family will be making a long car journey soon and the parent would like some advice on ways to prevent motion sickness. The child is not present.
TasksJson: ["Find out reason for parent\u0027s visit.","Explore effectiveness of any treatments tried (anti-nausea wrist bands, medication, etc.). Find out about any previous medical advice received.","Emphasise benefits of medication for motion sickness (e.g., effective management, age-appropriate, no side effects, not harmful to health, non-drowsy, etc.). Recommend consulting pharmacist (e.g., medication options, etc.). Find out about child\u0027s activities during car journeys.","Confirm reading contributes to motion sickness (e.g., looking down, multiple conflicting senses: inner ear and eyes, etc.). Make recommendations (e.g., fresh air, looking straight ahead, light meals before travelling, listening to audio books/music, sleep, regular breaks, keeping hydrated, etc.).","Reassure parent about motion sickness in older children (e.g., less common, easier management of symptoms, etc.). Find out about any other questions."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is 40 years old and has been referred by his/her doctor with suspected appendicitis.
Background: Your patient is 40 years old and has been referred by his/her doctor with suspected appendicitis. He/she is waiting to see a doctor.
TasksJson: ["Find out why patient has come to Emergency Department.","Find out details about pain (time frame, location, severity, other symptoms, etc.).","Explain next steps (e.g., examination by doctor, tests to confirm diagnosis, if surgery needed: IV/intravenous line, etc.).","Give procedure for ruptured appendix (e.g., urgent surgery: hospitalisation for a few days, etc.). Outline possible need for insertion of cannula (e.g., if laparoscopic surgery needed, small narrow tube, to inflate abdomen with carbon dioxide gas, enabling clearer view, etc.). Find out any other questions/concerns.","Resist request for pain killers (e.g., doctor examination first, etc.). Explore painkillers already taken (type, dosage, time frame, etc.).","Advise patient about likely waiting time (e.g., priority status, condition monitored, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: The patient is in hospital following a road accident. The patient's condition is stable but he/she has lost blood and needs a blood transfus
Background: The patient is in hospital following a road accident. The patient's condition is stable but he/she has lost blood and needs a blood transfusion. The patient does not understand what will happen. The patient is anxious about the procedure.
TasksJson: ["Find out about the patient\u0027s concerns.","Reassure the patient that the possibility of infection is very small (as care is taken to screen donors and test donated blood for possible infection).","Explain the procedure for a blood transfusion (e.g., sterile conditions, new syringes, nurses watch closely, etc.).","Stress that the patient really needs the transfusion in order to recover fully."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is 55 years old and you have come to insert a urinary catheter, which is necessary for his/her operation on a broken hip.
Background: Your patient is 55 years old and you have come to insert a urinary catheter, which is necessary for his/her operation on a broken hip.
TasksJson: ["Confirm reason for seeing patient (insertion of urinary catheter before hip operation). Find out patient\u0027s knowledge/experience of catheters.","Explore reasons for patient\u0027s anxiety (process of inserting catheter, pain, embarrassment, etc.).","Reassure patient about catheter insertion (e.g., use of numbing gel, quick, minimal pain, no discomfort once in place, etc.). Emphasise no cause for embarrassment (e.g., standard procedure, routine for nurses, etc.). Explain need for catheter for operation (e.g., keeping bladder empty, controlling bladder function, monitoring of urine output, etc.).","Describe timescale for catheter (e.g., usually 24-hours postoperative, dependent on: patient\u0027s condition, recovery, mobility, etc.). Find out any other concerns.","Confirm risk of infection from catheter (e.g., prevention: removal as soon as possible, plenty of fluids, regular monitoring by nurses, etc.). Establish patient\u0027s willingness to go ahead with catheter insertion."]

ScenarioTitle: The parent of a 12-year-old girl asks for your co-operation in answering questions about a convulsive seizure (epilepsy) and what to do if h
Background: The parent of a 12-year-old girl asks for your co-operation in answering questions about a convulsive seizure (epilepsy) and what to do if his/her daughter had another seizure following her discharge from hospital sometime later today. Its details will be in the local telephone book or on the internet."]

Background: Your patient is a 25-year-old who has been experiencing considerable pain and discomfort in the right foot.
TasksJson: ["Ask about patient\u2019s symptoms and duration of discomfort.","Explain the diagnosis and causes of plantar wart (viral infection, person to person transmission, absence of shoes at public places e.g. swimming pools, showers, etc.).","Outline choices of treatment: Liquid peeling medicine-salicylic acid (easy application, variable effectiveness, slow process). ScenarioTitle: A three-year-old child has been brought to hospital suffering from chest tightness, wheezing and dyspnoea.
Background: A three-year-old child has been brought to hospital suffering from chest tightness, wheezing and dyspnoea. You suspect the child has asthma. The parent is anxious and becomes agitated whilst the child is waiting to see a doctor. You are the nurse taking the child’s vital signs.

ScenarioTitle: You are an A & E nurse. A young man/woman has presented at A&E with thermal burn to his/her forehead.
Background: You are an A & E nurse. A young man/woman has presented at A&E with thermal burn to his/her forehead. He/She is hysterical and is demanding immediate medical attention
TasksJson: ["Explain the likely treatment (give an analgesic injection, ointment to prevent","Find out about the injury. infection, cover with gauze, painkillers for home).","Empathize with him/her about her concerns and explain the importance of healing wound first.","Outline the things he/she can do that home to enhance recovery and minimize scarring (keep it moisturized, covered, use a sunscreen, use aloe Vera gel, healthy diet and remain hydrated)","Reassure him/her about scarring (scars may fade over time, preventative care of wound at home to reduce scarring, if a scab develops don\u0027t pull it, plenty of cosmetic treatments available after burn has healed in about 3-6 weeks dermatologist to offer more information after wound has healed).","Ask the patient to come back in two weeks\u0027 time for review."]

ScenarioTitle: You see a parent who has brought his/her four-year-old daughter to the clinic because a rash has appeared on her arms and legs after playing
Background: You see a parent who has brought his/her four-year-old daughter to the clinic because a rash has appeared on her arms and legs after playing at the park.
