ScenarioTitle: You are an agency home care nurse. Your patient is an 85-year-old who lives alone.
Background: You are an agency home care nurse. Your patient is an 85-year-old who lives alone. He/she has recently been discharged from hospital after a skin graft to repair an ulcer on his/her lower left leg. You visit him/her three days a week to dress the wound and help with showering. He/she is usually very cheerful but today seems worried.
TasksJson: ["Find out how the patient is doing.","Acknowledge the importance of being independent and suggest that this may still be possible with additional help.","Reassure the patient that the Aged Care Assessment Team can assess his/her situation and explain what is available (e.g, meal delivery service, cleaning assistance, transport for shopping etc.).","Seek permission to arrange a home visit by the team.","Assure the patient that they have made a good decision and explore other possible assistance they may require.","Remind the patient that it is normal to require some assistance post-surgery."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is 70 years old and is recovering in hospital from coronary artery bypass graft surgery after having a heart attack.
Background: Your patient is 70 years old and is recovering in hospital from coronary artery bypass graft surgery after having a heart attack. The doctor has recommended a continuous intravenous infusion of analgesic through an infusion pump. You are seeing the patient to set up this device.
TasksJson: ["Confirm reason for seeing patient (setting up infusion pump). Find out how patient is feeling (pain, headaches, dizziness, nausea, etc.).","Reassure patient about pain (e.g., as expected, improvement over time, increased provision of pain relief with infusion pump, etc.). Find out patient\u0027s understanding of procedure for setting up infusion pump.","Outline procedure for setting up infusion pump (e.g., insertion of cannula into arm, pain relief medication delivered continuously, etc.). Find out any concerns.","Emphasise timescale for effect of pain relief (e.g., a few hours: gradual build-up, current pain relief continued until then, etc.). Give information about infusion pump (e.g., dose checked and managed by nursing staff, not controlled by patient, 24-hour cycles of medication, etc.).","Reassure patient about pain relief (e.g., low risk of dependency, short-term use only, return to oral medication in a few days, etc.). Establish patient\u0027s consent for insertion of needle/tube."]

ScenarioTitle: You are the visiting school nurse at Hastings Secondary School.
Background: You are the visiting school nurse at Hastings Secondary School.  You are seeing Richard Gibson, a grade 9 student who is obese. He does not participate in any physical activities at school or at home and consumes fast food and sugary beverages a lot. He feels sleepy while attending classes.
TasksJson: ["Have his body mass index measured","Ask about his lifestyle and routines","Encourage him to take up any sport or other physical activities","Make him aware about healthy lifestyle choices and also warns of the long impact of too much junk food.","Ask him to keep a tab of his weight every week and to see you a month later on your visit to the school"]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is 55 years old. He/she has End-stage Renal Disease (ESRD).
Background: Your patient is 55 years old. He/she has End-stage Renal Disease (ESRD). You see his/her health is steadily deteriorating. The patient is an inpatient on your Renal Ward and you notice he/she appears lonely and depressed. He/she requires dialysis three times per week and is a candidate for a renal transplant.
TasksJson: ["Ask the patient to tell you how he/she is feeling.","Encourage the patient to talk about his/her fears about the condition.","Inform the patient that without dialysis he/she would suffer more.","Reassure the patient that there is always hope a donor will be found in time.","Suggest that a counsellor be consulted to support the patient\u0027s decision to be listed as Not for Resuscitation (NFR).","Provide reassurance that, if he/she wants to put his/her request in writing, it is hospital policy for staff to respect that, and having the family present is important."]

ScenarioTitle: You see the parent of a six-year-old boy, who was recently diagnosed with asthma and now uses a reliever inhaler.
Background: You see the parent of a six-year-old boy, who was recently diagnosed with asthma and now uses a reliever inhaler. The parent wants to discuss his/her son's medication. The child is not present.
TasksJson: ["Find out reason for parent\u0027s visit. Find out more about child\u0027s asthma (any improvement, compliance with use of reliever inhaler, etc.).","Find out about parent\u0027s knowledge of different inhalers (e.g., preventer inhaler, etc.).","Give details of preventer inhalers (e.g., prophylactic: preventing inflammation of airways, regular use, etc.). Remind parent of details of reliever inhaler (e.g., reactive, reducing inflammation/swelling in airways, use as required, etc.).","Emphasise side effects of inhaled preventer medication/corticosteroids unlikely (e.g., low drug dose, prevented by use of spacer, etc.). Explain benefits of preventer use (e.g., developing long-term protection, etc.). Advise on frequency of use of preventer inhaler (e.g., twice daily, morning and evening, etc.). Find out any other questions/concerns.","Stress importance of child living normal life (e.g., staying active, appropriate use of reliever inhaler, etc.). Suggest another review (e.g., son to be present, in six weeks, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: This patient was brought into the emergency department of your hospital late last night suffering from an acute asthma attack.
Background: This patient was brought into the emergency department of your hospital late last night suffering from an acute asthma attack. He/she is currently being held for observation. The patient has had a fright and is very concerned about his/her condition.
TasksJson: ["Find out how the patient is feeling and if they have any questions about asthma.","Explain what asthma is (e.g., a chronic disease of the airways, etc.).","Discuss the causes, such as environmental factors and an inherited predisposition.","Explain the treatment, for example, a Ventolin (salbutamol) inhaler, and how to use such an inhaler.","Discuss the prognosis for asthma patients.","Deal with the patient\u2019s anxiety about the problem, emphasising that asthma can be controlled."]

ScenarioTitle: You are a Head Nurse. You are attending on a patient who has undergone an operation for thyroid gland removal.
Background: You are a Head Nurse. You are attending on a patient who has undergone an operation for thyroid gland removal. The patient is unable to speak properly and she has difficulty in swallowing or even breathing properly.
TasksJson: ["Begin with warm and friendly greetings.","Answer questions that she may ask","Assure her that problems related to speaking, swallowing, breathing will go away sooner (usually, they go away after 2-3 weeks)","Advice her not to pressurize her vocal chords by speaking continuously.","Suggest to elevate her head at all times for the first 4-5 days after surgery, even while sleeping."]

ScenarioTitle: An eighteen year old female with undiagnosed anorexia nervosa has presented to your emergency department with an abnormal heart rhythm cause
Background: An eighteen year old female with undiagnosed anorexia nervosa has presented to your emergency department with an abnormal heart rhythm caused by her poor nutritional status. Cardiac treatment has stabilised her heart but she is still currently receiving a potassium infusion via a drip to prevent further such problems. Other than when she wants you to explain treatment to her, she is defensive and angry to communicate with and in denial that she has any kind of eating disorder or mental health issues.
TasksJson: ["Reassuringly answer her anxious questions about the intravenous drip being given to stabilise her electrolytes.","Tactfully ask her about her eating habits and food intake, emphasising your therapeutic aims for asking these questions.","Advise her that a mental health doctor will come to see her soon and when she becomes angry about having to see a \u2018doctor for crazy people\u2019, try to persuade her of the importance of dealing with her mental health/eating issues to prevent such life threatening hospital admissions."]

ScenarioTitle: The patient is in hospital following a road accident. The patient's condition is stable but he/she has lost blood and needs a blood transfus
Background: The patient is in hospital following a road accident. The patient's condition is stable but he/she has lost blood and needs a blood transfusion. The patient does not understand what will happen. The patient is anxious about the procedure.
TasksJson: ["Find out about the patient\u0027s concerns.","Reassure the patient that the possibility of infection is very small (as care is taken to screen donors and test donated blood for possible infection).","Explain the procedure for a blood transfusion (0.9., sterile conditions, new Syringes, nurses watch closely, etc.).","Stress that the patient really needs the transfusion in order to recover fully."]

ScenarioTitle: You see the parent of a seven-year-old girl who has recently had a heavy nosebleed.
Background: You see the parent of a seven-year-old girl who has recently had a heavy nosebleed. The parent didn't know what to do and would like some advice in case it happens again. The daughter is not present.
TasksJson: ["Find out reason for parent\u0027s visit.","Find out details about child\u0027s nosebleed (amount of blood, duration, treatment given by parent, etc.). Explore relevant information about child (previous nosebleeds/injuries to nose, general health, medication, etc.).","Warn against leaning back (e.g., risk of choking on blood/suffocation, etc.). Advise on method to stop nosebleed (e.g., leaning forward with head tilted forward, pinching nose above nostrils 10\u201315 minutes, application of ice pack to top of nose, etc.).","Advise when medical attention needed (e.g., duration longer than 15 minutes, excessive blood loss, nosebleed following trauma, persistent nosebleeds, etc.). Give information about nosebleeds in children (e.g., regular occurrence in 50% of children aged 6\u201315 years, usually caused by: picking/blowing nose too hard, dryness in nose, etc.).","Suggest use of saline nasal spray (e.g., reduction in: dryness, irritation, soreness, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: You are an A & E nurse. A man has presented at A & E at 3am.
Background: You are an A & E nurse. A man has presented at A & E at 3am. He states his name is Joseph Groom. He has suffered a head injury and may have mild concussion. He also has cuts and bruises to his body, his right hand is swollen and his clothes are torn. He is intoxicated. He insists he wants something for pain relief while waiting to see the doctor.
TasksJson: ["Ask for details about what happened","Find out the extent of his injuries","Explain that you cannot administer pain relief before examination by a doctor","Explain that all medications have side effects and that in some cases these are exacerbated by alcohol","Try make him as comfortable as possible."]

ScenarioTitle: You are specifically assigned the duty of advising those with long-term conditions on smoking cessation and the effects this can have on the
Background: You are specifically assigned the duty of advising those with long-term conditions on smoking cessation and the effects this can have on their condition and treatment. You are meeting a 42 year old woman admitted with an exacerbation of chronic pulmonary disease. She leads a busy life, with an insurance job and a family of 3 children.
TasksJson: ["Explain the effect of smoking on long-term conditions","Increase the patient\u2019s confidence in using treatments to quit smoking while in hospital","Offer emotional and psychological support","Suggest other methods to reduce stress"]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 78-year-old who is in hospital after surgery to remove a large lesion from their back.
Background: Your patient is a 78-year-old who is in hospital after surgery to remove a large lesion from their back. He/she is recovering well, and you want him/her to get up to have a shower and do some exercise.
TasksJson: ["Find out the patient\u0027s current mood and ask to check the state of the wound.","Reassure the patient the wound site is healing well and emphasise it is now time to have a shower.","Promote the benefits of having a shower (e.g., feeling better, improved cleanliness, etc.).","Advise that a waterproof dressing will be placed over the wound.","Recommend the patient start doing gentle exercises (e.g., stretching, walking down the hall, etc.).","Stress the importance of exercise (e.g., faster recovery time, fewer aches and pains, enhanced mood, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: A 40 year old woman who is suffering from some urinary problems demands you to get a urologist to prescribe some anti-infalmmatory medicatio
Background: A 40 year old woman who is suffering from some urinary problems demands you to get a urologist to prescribe some anti-infalmmatory medications, but she feels shy to disclose in words what she has been exerpiencing, she is worried about being scoffed at.
TasksJson: ["Find out what problems exactly the patient has without being unfriendly or impolite","Reassure her and tell her of the possible causes and treatment available."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is 44 years old and preparing for discharge following episodes of syncope (fainting).
Background: Your patient is 44 years old and preparing for discharge following episodes of syncope (fainting). Assessments have ruled out any cardiac issues and indicate postural/orthostatic hypotension as the cause, due to cessation of blood pressure medication. You are seeing the patient to give instructions for blood pressure monitoring at home as advised by the doctor.
TasksJson: ["Explain reason for seeing patient (information about BP/blood pressure monitoring at home). Find out how patient is feeling.","Reassure patient about discharge decisions (e.g., made by multidisciplinary team, dependent on assessment, etc.). Find out patient\u0027s knowledge of BP monitoring.","Give information about taking BP readings (e.g., rolling up sleeve, resting arm on table with palm face up, locating pulse, securing cuff, inflating and deflating cuff, documenting readings, etc.). Describe timings of readings (e.g., twice daily, different times of day, for three weeks, etc.).","Advise patient on how to avoid fainting (e.g., not getting up quickly, regular fluid intake, lying down and elevating legs when dizzy, etc.). Find out about patient\u0027s support network (family, friends, etc.).","Emphasise importance of support (e.g., physical: avoiding prolonged standing; psychological: listening to worries/concerns; etc.). Advise need for review appointment in one week\u0027s time (checking BP, reviewing readings, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: You see the parent of a three-year-old child who has a buckle fracture of the right wrist.
Background: You see the parent of a three-year-old child who has a buckle fracture of the right wrist. The child has been given pain relief and had a removable splint put on. He is now ready for discharge. You see the parent to advise on aftercare. The child is not present for the discussion.
TasksJson: ["Confirm reason for seeing parent (information about aftercare). Find out how parent is feeling about child going home.","Advise need to continue pain relief (e.g., paracetamol/acetaminophen: regular doses for next 24 hours, etc.). Find out relevant details about child (if attending childcare centre, any siblings, etc.).","Stress importance of avoiding contact sports/rough play (e.g., prevention of further injury/increased pain, etc.). Find out parent\u0027s knowledge/experience of removable splints.","Confirm timing of removable splint use (e.g., three weeks: day and night, only removed for bathing, etc.). Outline need for parent to remove splint permanently in three weeks (e.g., re-applying if wrist sore/stiff/painful, etc.).","Reassure parent about removal of splint in three weeks (e.g., most likely: mended, no need for further use/medical attention, etc.). Advise when to see doctor (e.g., three weeks after injury: if wrist remains painful/swollen; after splint removal: if no/limited use of wrist/hand/fingers, increased pain/numbness, etc.). Find out about any other questions."]

ScenarioTitle: You see a 78-year-old patient who has been prescribed diuretics to alleviate oedema (water retention).
Background: You see a 78-year-old patient who has been prescribed diuretics to alleviate oedema (water retention). He/she wants to stop taking them because of side effects.
TasksJson: ["Find out reason for patient\u0027s visit.","Advise patient against stopping diuretics (e.g., prescribed for a reason, risk of damage to health, etc.). Explore reasons for patient\u0027s reluctance to continue with diuretics.","Find out relevant details about patient\u0027s routine (extent/timing of fluid intake, timing of medication, etc.).","Give information on effect of diuretic (e.g., duration: approx. six hours, etc.). Make recommendations about timing of medication (e.g., first dose early in day, second dose mid-afternoon: avoiding sleep disruption, etc.). Recommend when to have last fluid intake (e.g., at least two hours before bed, etc.). Find out more details about patient\u0027s headaches/dizziness (frequency, severity, etc.).","Advise need for urgent appointment with doctor (e.g., patient check-up, blood pressure check, discussion of alternative medication, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: You are speaking to a 49-year-old man/woman who has undergone a barium enema earlier today.
Background: You are speaking to a 49-year-old man/woman who has undergone a barium enema earlier today. He/She presented two days ago with complaints of abdominal discomfort and change in bowel habit. You have his test results which are unremarkable but notice that he/she looks angry.
TasksJson: ["Find out why the patient is angry","Ask if the patient is still experiencing any pain","Explain that enema is generally not painful for people and probably that is why he was not informed earlier. (patient might have sensitive bowel due to which it was painful)","Empathize with the patient","Explain that the purpose of performing the procedure was to examine his/her colon and rectum for cancer","Reassure the patient that his/her results are normal and the doctor will see him her shortly to prescribe medication for his complaints."]

ScenarioTitle: You see the parent of a ten-month-old baby boy. The child has a persistent rash on his buttocks.
Background: You see the parent of a ten-month-old baby boy. The child has a persistent rash on his buttocks. You have just examined the child and diagnose nappy/diaper rash. The child is not present for the discussion.
TasksJson: ["Confirm presence of nappy/diaper rash (e.g., severe case, common condition: not cause for concern, etc.). Outline next steps (e.g., discussion about changing routine, advice on prevention, etc.). Find out any questions/concerns.","Give reasons for your clinical opinion (e.g., nappy/diaper rash varies in severity, confined to baby\u0027s buttocks, no fever/other symptoms, etc.). Reassure parent about crying/difficulty sleeping (e.g., common in young babies, possibility of teething/colic, unlikely to be a concern, etc.). Make recommendations (e.g., monitoring baby, etc.).","Find out about nappy/diaper changing routine (frequency, type of nappies/diapers, use of soap/baby wipes, etc.).","Explore details about treatments tried for nappy/diaper rash (e.g., antiseptic creams, paracetamol/acetaminophen, etc.).","Describe common strategies for preventing rash (e.g., gentle cleansing of skin, barrier creams, avoiding: perfumed soap, baby wipes, etc.). Suggest short periods without nappy/diaper (e.g., breathing time for skin, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: This parent's six-year-old son has cut his finger, which is bleeding freely.
Background: This parent's six-year-old son has cut his finger, which is bleeding freely. You examine the cut, which is not too serious, and you don't think he needs stitches.
TasksJson: ["Find out how the cut happened.","Reassure the parent. Answer his/her questions about length of time for healing. any scarring, whether stitches are necessary, etc.","Explain how to clean, apply antiseptic, and dress the cut suitably. Point out the need to keep the finger clean and dry.","Warn the parent about keeping sharp implements out of reach. Be tactful in giving advice"]

ScenarioTitle: You are a nurse in an operating theatre recovery room. Your 80-year-old patient is recovering after hip replacement surgery.
Background: You are a nurse in an operating theatre recovery room. Your 80-year-old patient is recovering after hip replacement surgery. They are receiving IV fluids. They have been able to tell you their name but seem confused about where they are.
TasksJson: ["Explain their situation (recovery room, post surgery).","Check for awareness (orientation for time, place, person).","Advise them family are nearby (daughter in post-operative ward).","Explain hospital policy (no visitors in the recovery room).","Explain why they cannot have fluids by mouth at this stage (possible infection, pneumonia). Offer an ice cube to ease thirst.","Assure them that they will be taken back to their ward shortly."]

ScenarioTitle: You have been called to the patient's bedside. The patient was supposed to go in for his surgery at 10 am and was second on the list but sur
Background: You have been called to the patient's bedside. The patient was supposed to go in for his surgery at 10 am and was second on the list but surgery was delayed because the previous patient had some complications during surgery. Apparently he had never had an anesthesic before and was suffering from post op vomiting, hadn't passed urine and is in pain. The patient's daughter is very angry and wants to talk to you.
TasksJson: ["Find out why the patient\u0027s daughter is angry.","Empathise with the daughter about the delay but be realistic about how long the patient may have to wait.","Explain why the operation is late, try not to blame Theatre staff but explain post op complications can be unavoidable.","Negotiate with the daughter to prevent her from insisting her father is discharged."]

ScenarioTitle: You see a 52-year-old patient who is scheduled for an upper gastrointestinal (UGI) endoscopy to investigate his/her gastro-oesophageal reflu
Background: You see a 52-year-old patient who is scheduled for an upper gastrointestinal (UGI) endoscopy to investigate his/her gastro-oesophageal reflux (acid reflux). He/she wants more information about the procedure.
TasksJson: ["Find out how patient feels about endoscopy.","Give information about endoscopy (e.g., short duration: around 15 minutes; sedation provided; local anaesthetic throat spray to numb area; very little pain; some discomfort; etc.).","Describe preparation for procedure (e.g., no food after midnight, only clear liquids up to six hours beforehand, etc.). Find out about any current medication.","Emphasise need for pre-procedure fasting (e.g., risk of aspiration of food/drink into lungs under sedation, ensuring good view, etc.). Suggest what patient can have for breakfast on day (e.g., black coffee/tea, apple juice, etc.). Find out any other questions/concerns.","Reassure patient about procedure (e.g., complications: rare; monitoring before and after; more information available from doctor; etc.).","Explain what to expect post-procedure (e.g., mild discomfort in throat, need for rest, quick recovery and discharge, etc.). Explain aftereffects of sedation and throat spray (e.g., drowsiness, etc.). Stress need to arrange someone to take patient home (e.g., friend, relative, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: You see a 66-year-old patient who presents with xerostomia (a dry mouth), especially on waking.
Background: You see a 66-year-old patient who presents with xerostomia (a dry mouth), especially on waking. You give the patient advice on managing the condition.
TasksJson: ["Find out reason for patient\u0027s visit.","Find out relevant patient details (condition of tongue/lips, bad breath, any trouble swallowing/chewing, if a smoker, etc.).","Outline possible causes of xerostomia/dry mouth (e.g., lack of saliva production, age, breathing through mouth at night, dehydration, some medications, etc.). Find out about any current medication.","Make recommendations to relieve xerostomia (e.g., keeping mouth moist, using alcohol-free mouthwash, limiting salt/sugar intake, humidifier in bedroom, etc.).","Stress need for doctor appointment only if symptoms continue/get worse (e.g., doctor to discuss other options for treatment/medication, etc.). Emphasise importance of regular dental check-ups (e.g., dry mouth possible cause of: tooth decay, dental issues, mouth infections, etc.). Establish patient\u0027s consent for examination."]

ScenarioTitle: You are speaking to a 45-year-old woman who has been admitted to the hospital with a suspected stroke.
Background: You are speaking to a 45-year-old woman who has been admitted to the hospital with a suspected stroke. You have been asked by the doctor to administer a Warfarin injection (anti-coagulant) to the patient.
TasksJson: ["Take the medical history of the patient before giving the injection.","Explain that after the injection, Warfarin needs to be taken in tablet form every day for the next four weeks.","Explain that you need to check with the doctor if she can continue her herbal supplement (it may interfere with Warfarin or cause side effects)","Emphasize the importance of cautionary measures regarding Warfarin (minimize Vitamin K in diet, avoid OTC medicines due to their interaction with Warfarin, take a dose at the same time each day)","Offer to provide a detailed patient information leaflet on Warfarin","Advise the patient to stop the medication and contact the doctor immediately in case of unusual or prolonged bleeding"]

ScenarioTitle: A three-year-old girl has come with her parent to be admitted with an ear abscess.
Background: A three-year-old girl has come with her parent to be admitted with an ear abscess. Her parent is anxious about how she will settle in. You need information about the child's normal routine and habits in order to prepare a nursing care plan.
TasksJson: ["Confirm the reason for admission and find out the parent\u0027s concerns.","Reassure the parent about the care their daughter will receive (constant monitoring, checking to ensure her needs are being met, etc.).","Find out if the daughter has any siblings. Assure the parent that she will have other children to play with during her stay.","Explore his/her daughter\u0027s routine (e.g., usual bedtime, naps, meal times and food preferences, toileting, etc.). Check if his/her daughter has brought a comfort item with her.","Outline visiting hours are from 11am to 8pm, but stress that overnight stays are possible in a special visiting room."]

ScenarioTitle: You see a 75-year-old patient who is concerned because he/she has recently been having trouble getting to the bathroom quickly enough: he/sh
Background: You see a 75-year-old patient who is concerned because he/she has recently been having trouble getting to the bathroom quickly enough: he/she is having issues with urinary incontinence. He/she doesn't have a temperature or any other symptoms. The patient would like some advice.
TasksJson: ["Find out reason for patient\u0027s visit.","Find out more details about patient\u0027s incontinence (onset, frequency, amount of urine, day/night occurrence, previous occurrences, etc.). Explore any changes in patient\u0027s bladder habits (frequency of passing urine, pain passing urine, etc.).","Explore further relevant patient details (general health, any history of bladder conditions, current infections/constipation, long-term medication, etc.).","Give common reasons for incontinence (e.g., infection, constipation, bladder irritation due to diet, etc.). Recommend doctor\u0027s appointment (e.g., physical examination, blood tests, analysis of urine sample, etc.). Find out any questions/concerns.","Reassure patient about his/her condition (e.g., very common, no need for embarrassment, can be resolved/managed, etc.). Advise on management of condition (e.g., pelvic muscle exercise, scheduled toileting, incontinence pads, avoiding caffeine, increasing water intake, double voiding: passing urine more than once, etc.). Establish patient\u0027s willingness to make doctor\u0027s appointment."]

ScenarioTitle: You are speaking to a 40-year-old man/woman who has come to the clinic for routine check-up.
Background: You are speaking to a 40-year-old man/woman who has come to the clinic for routine check-up. He/She is travelling overseas next month with work, and the General Practitioner has asked you to advise him/her on recommended travel immunizations prior to international travel.
TasksJson: ["Find out about his/her vaccination history (tetanus, hepatitis A, and influenza/flu) and the duration of his travel.","Explain that he/she needs to get vaccinated against typhoid, hepatitis A, and tetanus (recommended by WHO for travelers to Cambodia and Vietnam medium risk countries).","Explain and emphasize the importance of getting his/her vaccinations updated at least two weeks prior to travelling abroad (tetanus can be fatal, and vaccination needs to be administered once in every ten years, a combined vaccination can be given for hepatitis A and typhoid now and a booster after six months).","Reassure him/her that the vaccinations are not painful and are generally well"]

ScenarioTitle: You see a 24-year-old patient who was recently diagnosed with fibromyalgia (a chronic condition that causes pain and fatigue) and prescribed
Background: You see a 24-year-old patient who was recently diagnosed with fibromyalgia (a chronic condition that causes pain and fatigue) and prescribed analgesia medication and relaxation techniques for symptom relief. This appointment is to review his/her condition and medication.
TasksJson: ["Confirm reason for patient\u0027s visit (review following fibromyalgia diagnosis). Find out about effectiveness of analgesia medication (any changes: in pain, energy levels, side effects, etc.).","Find out more details about patient\u0027s pains (location, possible triggers, duration, etc.). Explore effectiveness of pain management (analgesia, relaxation techniques, etc.).","Make recommendations to address pain (e.g., paracetamol/acetaminophen four times per day, doctor appointment to discuss analgesia, pain diary to identify triggers, etc.). Find out about patient\u0027s exercise regime.","Emphasise benefits of regular exercise for fibromyalgia (e.g., controlling/reducing pain, building muscle strength, improving: energy levels, stamina, mental health, etc.). Recommend low-impact exercise (e.g., swimming, water aerobics, etc.). Find out patient\u0027s experience/knowledge of fibromyalgia support groups.","Stress benefits of joining support group (e.g., shared experience, understanding, advice, etc.). Remind patient of next review (in three months, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is 40 years old and was admitted to hospital yesterday morning suffering from a chest infection.
Background: Your patient is 40 years old and was admitted to hospital yesterday morning suffering from a chest infection. He/she has asked to speak to you.
TasksJson: ["Find out how patient is feeling. Find out any questions/concerns.","Emphasise need to remain in hospital (e.g., unresolved chest infection, danger of infection worsening: leading to longer stay in hospital, etc.). Explore options for help with childcare.","Advise patient of next steps (insertion of cannula, administering appropriate medication, monitoring recovery, etc.). Find out any other questions/concerns.","Give information about cannula (e.g., needle in vein, removal of needle leaving small tube in place, etc.).","Resist request for oral antibiotics (e.g., severity of infection, intravenous antibiotics preferable to tablets: immediate entry to bloodstream, quick procedure, etc.). Offer topical anaesthetic (e.g., numbing area, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: You are a community nurse and you are making one of your regular home visits to a 75-year-old patient with Parkinson's disease.
Background: You are a community nurse and you are making one of your regular home visits to a 75-year-old patient with Parkinson's disease.
TasksJson: ["Find out how patient has been since last visit. Explore effectiveness of medication.","Find out more relevant patient details (level of fatigue, sleeping patterns, etc.).","Give information about patient\u0027s urinary problems (urge incontinence: sudden and strong urge to urinate; nocturia: waking often to urinate; common; etc.). Find out more details (any daytime urgency, any particular triggers, effect on mood, etc.).","Explain cause of urge incontinence in Parkinson\u0027s patients (e.g., disruption of messages from brain to bladder, inadequate muscle relaxation when urinating, incomplete emptying of bladder, etc.).","Reassure patient about self-help measures (e.g., effective: emptying bladder before bedtime, balanced diet, avoidance of caffeine/alcohol/fizzy drinks, incontinence products, etc.). Advise patient to see doctor if problem persists (e.g., discussion of other options, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 60-year-old who has come to see their Doctor for a six-monthly check-up.
Background: Your patient is a 60-year-old who has come to see their Doctor for a six-monthly check-up. Unfortunately, there have been a number of medical emergencies today and as a result, the clinic is running behind schedule. Your patient has approached you and seems quite angry.
TasksJson: ["Find out the patient\u0027s concerns.","Apologise for the wait. Explain that there have been some medical emergencies resulting in delays.","Explain the Doctor is working as fast as they can, and they will see patients as soon as possible.","Express concern about the patient\u0027s threatening behaviour. Explain such behaviour will not be tolerated and that security may have to be called if the patient does not calm down.","Reassure the patient that it won\u0027t be much longer. Ask them if they would like a cup of tea or some water in the meantime."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 54-year-old who has a provisional diagnosis of sleep apnoea.
Background: Your patient is a 54-year-old who has a provisional diagnosis of sleep apnoea. The patient’s doctor has referred him/her to you to discuss the sleep study.
TasksJson: ["Confirm patient is at the clinic for sleep study information and explain how the monitoring is done (placement of sensors on head, chest and limbs to measure breathing rates and snoring).","Tell patient about possible implications of the sensors (discomfort, sleep disruption). Find out if patient has any more concerns about the study.","Reassure patient that he/she is able to take a sleeping tablet before the test. Inform patient about the availability of a home sleep study. Confirm patient\u2019s preference.","Explain main treatment for sleep apnoea (CPAP continuous positive airways pressure delivered via face mask to keep airway open) and lifestyle changes (lose weight, avoid alcohol, etc.). Check patient\u0027s willingness to comply.","Explain effects of excess weight around the throat (causes airway restriction) and emphasise the benefits of weight loss (less daytime sleepiness, decreased snoring, reduced blood pressure, less risk of heart attack) and refer patient to a dietician."]

ScenarioTitle: You are taking care of a 60-year-old patient who has an AKI (acute kidney injury, also known as acute renal failure/ARF).
Background: You are taking care of a 60-year-old patient who has an AKI (acute kidney injury, also known as acute renal failure/ARF). He/she has been given fluids and had blood tests.
TasksJson: ["Find out how patient is feeling.","Find out patient\u0027s reasons for wanting to be discharged.","Explain why immediate discharge is not advisable (e.g., more fluids required: one more day minimum; awaiting blood results; importance of monitoring AKI/acute kidney injury; etc.).","Emphasise that self-discharge is not recommended (e.g., worsening condition, possible complications, bladder damage, kidney failure, etc.). Explore alternative care arrangements for his/her spouse (family, friends, etc.).","Reassure patient about discharge (e.g., as soon as possible, lengthy stay unlikely, etc.). Find out if patient has any other concerns.","Stress importance of self-care to avoid future admissions to hospital (e.g., good hydration, balanced diet, respite care for spouse, avoiding medications such as ibuprofen and other NSAIDs/nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: You are a nurse in an operating theatre recovery room. 80-year-old Doris Mack is recovering after hip replacement surgery.
Background: You are a nurse in an operating theatre recovery room. 80-year-old Doris Mack is recovering after hip replacement surgery. She is receiving IV fluids. She has been able to tell you her name but seems confused about where she is. She keeps asking to see her daughter and to have a cup of tea.
TasksJson: ["Explain her situation","Check for understanding","Re-explain if necessary","Advise her that her daughter is waiting to see her in the post-operative ward","Explain that hospital policy excludes visitors from the recovery room","Explain why she cannot have fluids by mouth at this stage","Assure her that she will be taken back to her ward shortly and then her needs will be attended to based on the doctor\u0027s orders."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 19-year-old university student with itchy eyes.
Background: Your patient is a 19-year-old university student with itchy eyes. You have just examined the patient and cleaned the eyes with a mild saline solution. There is crusting of the eyelids and lashes. You suspect conjunctivitis.
TasksJson: ["Find out more about eye problem (onset, duration of problem, any discharge, level of severity/discomfort, etc.).","Give conjunctivitis as likely cause (common non-traumatic eye complaint: irritation, discharge; possible causes: virus, bacteria, allergy; etc.).","Reassure student about conjunctivitis (e.g., if treated effectively: no adverse effect on vision, etc.). Advise patient to visit doctor (e.g., confirmation of diagnosis, possible need for antibiotics, etc.).","Confirm possibility of contagiousness of conjunctivitis (e.g., early diagnosis and treatment: limiting spread, etc.). Emphasise need to avoid contaminating other people (e.g., hygiene practices: strict hand washing, frequent linen change, etc.). Find out if patient wears contact lenses.","Emphasise contact lenses are not to be worn with conjunctivitis (e.g., until any treatment complete, etc.). Recommend symptom relief (e.g., cleaning eyelids with wet cloth, cold/warm compresses: several times daily, etc.). Find out any other questions/concerns."]

ScenarioTitle: Your 32 year old patient was diagnosed with bi-polar disorder, when conducting a therapy session, you find out that the patient is not compl
Background: Your 32 year old patient was diagnosed with bi-polar disorder, when conducting a therapy session, you find out that the patient is not complying with medication regimen.
TasksJson: ["Discuss the condition with the patient","Find out details about non-compliance","Offer solutions to the problems."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is 65 years old and has come to the clinic for the annual flu vaccination.
Background: Your patient is 65 years old and has come to the clinic for the annual flu vaccination. He/she is uncertain about having the vaccination.
TasksJson: ["Confirm reason for appointment (flu vaccination/shot). Find out any questions or concerns.","Explore reasons for patient\u0027s reluctance to have flu vaccination.","Outline reasons for having flu vaccination (e.g., stimulation of body\u0027s immune system, production of antibodies, reduction of risk of flu by 40\u201360%, reduction in severity of symptoms if contracted, etc.). Find out about flu vaccination history.","Reassure patient about side effects (e.g., mild: headache, fever, nausea, muscle ache; relieved with paracetamol/acetaminophen; duration of 1\u20132 days; etc.).","Emphasise possible consequences of contracting flu without vaccination (e.g., inflammation of lungs, respiratory failure, etc.). Stress importance of having vaccination (e.g., risk reduction rather than risk elimination, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: You see a parent who has brought his/her two-year-old son to the Emergency Department because he has swallowed a button.
Background: You see a parent who has brought his/her two-year-old son to the Emergency Department because he has swallowed a button. You are going to see the child in triage but are talking to the parent first. The child is not present for the discussion.
TasksJson: ["Find out reason for child\u0027s visit to Emergency Department.","Explore any physical effects on child (nausea, vomiting, fever, stomach ache, etc.). Find out more details about child\u0027s ingestion (how long ago, size and material of button, any action by parent, any food/drink since, etc.).","Explain next steps (e.g., vital signs to be taken, returning to waiting area, examination by doctor, decision on appropriate treatment, etc.). Find out any questions/concerns.","Resist giving waiting time (e.g., dependent on priority cases/availability of doctors, child stable, no airway problem, etc.).","Emphasise child not priority case (e.g., no physical symptoms/signs of distress, no risk of damage/internal bleeding, button likely to pass through system naturally, etc.). Establish parent\u0027s consent for you to take child\u0027s vital signs."]

ScenarioTitle: This patient was brought into the emergency department of your hospital late last night suffering from an acute asthma attack.
Background: This patient was brought into the emergency department of your hospital late last night suffering from an acute asthma attack. He/she is currently being held for observation. The patient has had a fright and is very concerned about his/her condition
TasksJson: ["Find out how the patient is feeling and if they have any questions about asthma","Explain what asthma is (e.g., a chronic disease of the airways, etc.).","Discuss the causes, such as environmental factors and an inherited predisposition.","Explain the treatment, for example, a Ventolin (salbutamol) inhaler, and how to use such an inhaler.","Discuss the prognosis for asthma patients.","Deal with the patient\u0027s anxiety about the problem; emphasizing that asthma can be controlled."]

ScenarioTitle: The concerned parent of a 6-year-old boy is seeking advice regarding their son’s recent episode of anaphylactic shock.
Background: The concerned parent of a 6-year-old boy is seeking advice regarding their son’s recent episode of anaphylactic shock. The attack occurred yesterday after eating a meal at a friend’s house. The boy is now ready to be discharged.
TasksJson: ["Reassure the parent that the boy has now completely recovered.","Outline what happens in the body (i.e., the immune system over-reacts to an allergen). Clarify which allergens are typically triggers (e.g. some foods [most commonly nuts, eggs, milk etc.], bee stings, certain medications [antibiotics, aspirin, etc.]).","Clarify that test results indicate that it is probably due to a peanut allergy.","Explain the importance of informing the school, teachers, relatives and friends. Advise checking all products likely to be consumed by the son for traces of peanuts.","Describe common symptoms (e.g. abdominal pain, confusion, facial swelling, etc.).","Reassure that the child may grow out of the allergy."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 67-year-old diabetic who is attending the clinic with an inflamed and swollen left foot caused by a cut to the small toe.
Background: Your patient is a 67-year-old diabetic who is attending the clinic with an inflamed and swollen left foot caused by a cut to the small toe. He/she is seeking medical advice and treatment.
TasksJson: ["Ask about the patient\u2019s presenting foot symptoms and how the cut occurred.","Explain the risks of delayed treatment (serious infection, ulceration, rare cases amputation, etc.).","Explain reasons for diabetic foot problems (poor wound healing, poor circulation, lack of feeling in feet, etc.). Reassure patient about the availability of medical treatment (antibiotics, dressings, pressure off-loading, etc.).","Explain importance of proper shoe fit (avoid friction, pressure sores, infection, etc.) and ask about the comfort and style of patient\u2019s footwear.","Recommend specialist footwear advice. Give instructions about essential foot care for diabetics (daily inspection of feet, observation for cuts, blisters and swelling, daily hygiene, trimmed toe nails, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: You see the parent of a six-year-old girl who has been having a lot of headaches.
Background: You see the parent of a six-year-old girl who has been having a lot of headaches. They don't seem to last very long, and the child seems fine afterwards. The parent doesn't think they are anything to worry about but would like some advice. The child is not present.
TasksJson: ["Find out reason for parent\u0027s visit.","Find out more details about child\u0027s headaches (onset, frequency/duration, time of day, area of head affected, level of pain, any nausea, any treatments tried, etc.).","Give information about headaches in children (e.g., usually tension headaches, not generally cause for concern, possibly genetic, etc.). Outline possible triggers (tiredness, insufficient food/fluid intake, excess screen time, change of routine/diet, etc.). Explore relevance of these to child.","Advise on prevention of headaches (e.g., consistent: sleep, eating, exercise routines; hydration/relaxation; screen time reduction before bed; etc.). Make further recommendations (e.g., headache diary for identification of specific triggers, etc.). Suggest doctor\u0027s appointment for child (e.g., ruling out underlying causes, etc.).","Reassure parent about doctor\u0027s appointment (e.g., precaution, providing reassurance, further advice, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is the parent of a 7-week-old baby boy. The baby has been bottle feeding well but has been frequently vomiting small amounts of
Background: Your patient is the parent of a 7-week-old baby boy. The baby has been bottle feeding well but has been frequently vomiting small amounts of milk and crying after feeds. The patient is worried that the baby has an illness and is very anxious to get advice and treatment for his/her son.
TasksJson: ["Ask the patient about his/her concerns for baby.","Explore the baby\u2019s feeding patterns.","Explain your diagnosis of reflux (i.e., gastro-oesophageal reflux, when baby brings up contents of stomach). Reassure that most babies with reflux are healthy.","Briefly describe the causes of reflux (undeveloped valve where food pipe joins the stomach, valve not strong enough to keep food/milk down).","Describe the ways to avoid reflux (feed baby in upright position, hold baby upright for 30 minutes after feeds, give smaller more frequent feeds, etc.).","Reassure the patient that their baby is not sick, reflux is common in babies, and it will disappear with time and by doing what was discussed."]

ScenarioTitle: Your 20-year-old patient is going to be travelling around Africa to do work experience for three months in a few months' time.
Background: Your 20-year-old patient is going to be travelling around Africa to do work experience for three months in a few months' time. He/she has read about taking antimalarial tablets, but doesn't want to take them so sees you to check if they are really necessary.
TasksJson: ["Find out reason for patient\u0027s visit.","Find out relevant patient details (any medication, medical conditions, etc.). Explore patient\u0027s reluctance towards antimalarial tablets (previous problems, side effects, length of time needed, etc.).","Emphasise range of antimalarial tablets available (e.g., variation in duration/side effects, advice given for patient selection, etc.).","Warn of limited effectiveness of other methods (e.g., no guarantee of complete protection, best used with medication, etc.). Give information about malaria (e.g., severe/recurrent condition, risk of serious complications, etc.). Find out details about patient\u0027s work experience (departure date, type of work, rural/urban location, etc.).","Recommend antimalarial tablets (e.g., reduction of risk of malaria: approx. 90%, etc.). Advise need for further appointment 8\u201312 weeks before departure (e.g., checking vaccination history, vaccinations, further guidance on antimalarial tablets, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: You see a 35-year-old patient who was stung by a wasp on the inside of his/her arm a couple of days ago.
Background: You see a 35-year-old patient who was stung by a wasp on the inside of his/her arm a couple of days ago. You have just examined the arm and the area around the sting is red, swollen and painful. You advise the patient it is a large local sting reaction and not a cause for concern.
TasksJson: ["Give findings of examination (some swelling, large local sting). Find out about any previous wasp stings. Explore any other symptoms (itchiness, wheezing, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness, etc.).","Reassure patient about reaction (e.g., no cause for concern, self-resolving after approx. one week, etc.). Give information about wasp stings (e.g., different levels of reaction, full reaction usually after 2\u20133 days, etc.).","Emphasise anaphylactic shock is usually immediate (e.g., rare, severe symptoms, etc.). Find out about any self-treatment.","Give details of self-care to relieve symptoms (e.g., painkillers, creams for itching, antihistamines, cold compress, avoiding scratching, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is 28 years old and has just had laparoscopic day surgery for a cholecystectomy (gallbladder removal) under general anaesthetic
Background: Your patient is 28 years old and has just had laparoscopic day surgery for a cholecystectomy (gallbladder removal) under general anaesthetic. You are seeing the patient to check on his/her progress.
TasksJson: ["Explain reason for visit (check on progress). Find out how patient is feeling after operation (any pain, nausea, etc.).","Reassure patient about side effects (e.g., result of anaesthetic: normal, temporary, etc.). Give information about pain relief (e.g., already given, time needed to take effect, to be increased if necessary, etc.). Emphasise need for patient to advise nursing staff of any changes (e.g., in pain/nausea, etc.).","Explain next steps (e.g., visit by doctor, discharge after 3\u20134 hours if urine is passed, etc.). Find out if patient is ready to eat/drink.","Outline possible aftereffects of surgery on digestive system (e.g., bloating, flatulence, diarrhoea, etc.). Encourage patient to drink (e.g., important for: settling stomach, recovery, hydration, discharge from hospital, etc.).","Stress no need for removal of stitches (e.g., dissolvable: disappear within two weeks; dressings: removal in 3\u20134 days; etc.). Find out about patient\u0027s discharge arrangements (someone to accompany patient home, carer at home for first 24 hours, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: You see a 25-year-old patient who has been diagnosed with epilepsy.
Background: You see a 25-year-old patient who has been diagnosed with epilepsy. You are doing a review of his/her symptoms and medication (carbamazepine).
TasksJson: ["Find out how patient has been coping since starting medication.","Explore differences in patient\u0027s symptoms pre- and post-medication (frequency, severity, etc.).","Confirm medication is working as expected (e.g., correct dosage, more effective over time, etc.). Find out if patient has any concerns.","Find out more about side effects of his/her medication (dry mouth, dizziness, headaches, blurred vision, etc.).","Reassure patient about side effects (e.g., common, disappear after a few weeks, not a concern, etc.). Make recommendations for if headaches persist (e.g., pain relief, etc.). Make suggestions for dry mouth (e.g., sugar-free gum, water, etc.).","Emphasise importance of continuing medication (e.g., until doctor\u0027s review in one month, etc.). Advise patient of options if no improvement in side effects (e.g., amending dosage, alternative medication, etc.). Recommend doctor appointment if symptoms get worse (e.g., unsteadiness, poor concentration, vomiting, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: You are a child welfare nurse. A young parent has brought his/her first child, an 18-month-old son named Jack, to see you.
Background: You are a child welfare nurse. A young parent has brought his/her first child, an 18-month-old son named Jack, to see you. Jack has always been a very contented baby but during the last few days he has been quite upset and crying. His parent is worried.
TasksJson: ["Find out the parent\u2019s concerns.","Suggest giving Jack a quick examination.","Tell his parent his gum is inflamed, and he is cutting his first molar tooth. Reassure the parent that teething problems usually settle quickly.","Outline supermarket products to ease the pain (teething ring, piece of apple, etc.).","Advise  consulting the chemist about teething gel and paracetamol oral suspension as necessary to relieve pain. Emphasize that the paracetamol dose is weight dependent."]

ScenarioTitle: You are speaking to a 25-year old man/woman who has presented himself/herself He/she looks very uncomfortable.
Background:
You are speaking to a 25-year old man/woman who has presented himself/herself
He/she looks very uncomfortable.
TasksJson: ["Find out the reason for the patient\u0027s visit","When the patient demands medication for migraine treatment, ask whether the patient has been clinically diagnosed with a migraine","Take a relevant history of the patient\u0027s condition (the type of pain, pain score, other symptoms)","Explain that he/she needs to see the doctor who would meet the patient after 30 minutes","Explain the risks involved in self-diagnosis/self-treatment","Emphasize the importance of getting a confirmed diagnosis from the doctor"]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is 55 years old and is due to be discharged following a knee procedure to repair a meniscal tear.
Background: Your patient is 55 years old and is due to be discharged following a knee procedure to repair a meniscal tear. You see the patient to give post-discharge information on recovery and wound care.
TasksJson: ["Confirm patient is due for discharge. Give reason for your visit (information on recovery/wound care). Find out how patient feels (any pain, discomfort, etc.).","Confirm aftereffects of operation/anaesthetic are common (e.g., tiredness, light-headedness: improvement in 48 hours, etc.). Describe expected post-operation knee symptoms (e.g., pain/swelling: gradual reduction, 1\u201312 weeks, etc.). Explain how to manage pain/swelling (e.g., elevation of leg, cold compress, painkillers, etc.).","Advise on wound care (e.g., keeping dressing dry/covered, replacing if wet/falls off, removing dressing after five days, etc.). Remind patient about stitches (e.g., dissolvable, no need for removal, etc.). Describe signs of infection requiring medical attention (e.g., increased pain, redness at wound site, high temperature, etc.).","Find out if patient has someone to accompany him/her home (to stay first 24 hours, help with practical tasks/shopping, etc.).","Emphasise need for support post-discharge (e.g., patient\u0027s restricted mobility/weight-bearing, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient, Harry Jones aged 78, is in hospital after surgery to remove a large lesion from his back.
Background: Your patient, Harry Jones aged 78, is in hospital after surgery to remove a large lesion from his back. He is recovering well and you want him to get up and walk about and to have a shower. You have observed that he has neglected his personal hygiene and appearance.
TasksJson: ["Encourage the patient to have a shower, wash his hair and generally get cleaned up. Be tactful as he can be quite cranky if he doesn\u2019t want to do something.","Say you will place a waterproof dressing over the lesion area.","Stress the importance of exercise and good hygiene in ensuring a speedy recovery."]

ScenarioTitle: Your 45 year old patient has come to the hospital for investigation of abdominal pain which began a few weeks ago.
Background: Your 45 year old patient has come to the hospital for investigation of abdominal pain which began a few weeks ago. She is extremely nervous about the tests and afraid that she may have cancer
TasksJson: ["Find out why the patient is feeling so anxious","Make some suggestions as to what the pain may be (indigestion, gall stones, irritable bowel, ulcer etc.)","Explain some of the tests to the patients, (gastroscopy, barium meal etc.)","Reassure the patient."]

ScenarioTitle: You are employed by a large interstate road transport company as an Occupational Health and Safety Nurse.
Background: You are employed by a large interstate road transport company as an Occupational Health and Safety Nurse. The company encourages staff to see you about any health concerns. The service is free and confidential. A truck driver aged 45 has come to see you. Weight 82 kg Ht 178 BP check 150 /90.
TasksJson: ["Ask about his health concerns.","Ask about his lifestyle ie diet, exercise smoking/drinking habits.","Check when he last visited a GP.","Advise BP indicates borderline hypertension and should be checked regularly.","Stress importance of commencing regular check- ups with GP.","Recommend:","reducing weight by healthy eating habits \u2013 less fat and less salt.","reducing alcohol intake.","30 minutes exercise 4-5 times a week."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a busy 50-year-old waitress, recently diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes.
Background: Your patient is a busy 50-year-old waitress, recently diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes. The patient had a wedge resection 12 days ago and has post-operative staphylococcus aureus (staph infection, non-MRSA) on the right large toe. You are visiting the home to change the dressing whilst the patient is resting from work duties.
TasksJson: ["Find out about the patient\u2019s general dialy habits after the operation. Did the patient rest adequately?","Highlight the fact that sometimes people get post operative infection but it is not really their fault.","Persuade your client to be patient and that the toe will heal with attendance to dressings, fresh air and daily exposure to the sun, antibiotics, etc.","Explain the risk of circulation problems for diabetes and sometimes greater risk of infection.","Supply a patient information brochure to the patient and agree to call again next week."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is 60 years old and is scheduled to have heart surgery in a few weeks.
Background: Your patient is 60 years old and is scheduled to have heart surgery in a few weeks. You have just completed the preoperative assessment, which was satisfactory.
TasksJson: ["Confirm preoperative assessment complete (all satisfactory, no cause for concern). Find out how patient is feeling about his/her stay in hospital.","Emphasise reasons for stay in intensive care (e.g., routine procedure after heart surgery, close monitoring, specialist medical staff, one-to-one care, etc.).","Resist request to give specific timescale for intensive care (e.g., decision by medical team, dependent on operation/recovery, etc.). Explain usual requirements for transfer to regular ward (e.g., patient stable: less need for medication, etc.).","Confirm visits allowed/encouraged (e.g., intensive care restrictions: due to patient welfare, limit number of visitors/duration of visit, etc.). Find out about patient\u0027s ideas for passing time during hospital stay.","Recommend use of headphones for noise elimination (e.g., machines, staff, visitors, patients, etc.). Find out about any other questions/concerns."]

ScenarioTitle: You are speaking to the mother of a 6-year-old boy, Jimmy, who was brought to the hospital this morning with a 2-week history of headaches a
Background: You are speaking to the mother of a 6-year-old boy, Jimmy, who was brought to the hospital this morning with a 2-week history of headaches and vomiting. The doctor ordered an MRI scan which revealed a tumor at the back of his brain on the right side. The patient had to be sedated before the MRI scan to remain still during the procedure due to which MRI took longer time. At present, he's under observation. He has been admitted to the hospital for a surgery. The doctor has informed the mother about the MRI results and surgery. She is distressed and completely shocked with this information.
TasksJson: ["Empathize with the mother and reassure her about her son\u0027s recovery.","Explain why the MRI was delayed and tell her that she will be able to see her son shortly.","When asked, explain that surgery is safe and her son\u0027s pain will be managed with medication.","Respond in a positive way to mother\u0027s questions about reoccurrence of a tumor (doctor believes a tumor is noncancerous, not likely to return, MRI tests after operation for some months for monitoring) and potential problems after the surgery (possibility of problems with physical abilities or behavior, or speech difficulties).","Reassure her about follow-up care after discharge (Occupational Therapists, connecting with caregivers).","Physical therapists, speech therapists, and Visiting Nurses, support group for","Encourage her to look after herself and not feel guilty about her son\u0027s condition."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is 45 years old and is due to have colorectal excision surgery (partial bowel removal) in order to treat cancer.
Background: Your patient is 45 years old and is due to have colorectal excision surgery (partial bowel removal) in order to treat cancer. The surgery has been delayed and the patient has asked to speak to you as he/she has some concerns.
TasksJson: ["Find out reason for patient\u0027s request to see you.","Apologise for delay (e.g., priority for emergency cases, elective cases not priority, etc.). Resist request for food (e.g., patient nil-by-mouth: prevention of nausea/aspiration of food during surgery, etc.). Explain when food will be provided (e.g., post-surgery, etc.).","Explore patient\u0027s reasons for wanting postponement of operation (e.g., any concerns about: procedure, aftereffects, anaesthetic, etc.).","Reassure patient about smoking (e.g., small number of cigarettes, unlikely to be an issue, etc.). Explain need to consult with anaesthetist (e.g., inform about smoking, make final decision on surgery, etc.). Outline risks of delaying surgery (e.g., less successful outcome, possible spread of cancer, etc.).","Reassure patient about your role (e.g., responding to questions/needs, providing reassurance, etc.). Find out any other concerns."]

ScenarioTitle: You have been called to the patient's bedside. The patient is a 37-year-old man/woman who were admitted to the hospital yesterday with a fra
Background: You have been called to the patient's bedside. The patient is a 37-year-old man/woman who were admitted to the hospital yesterday with a fractured leg. You notice that he/she looks quite agitated. It's early morning, and the doctor is on rounds in the hospital. He/She was given a painkiller earlier today.
TasksJson: ["Find out why the patient is angry","Explain that you were attending to a critical patient","Empathize with the patient regarding his/her complaint(s) and calm the patient down.","Ask him/her about the pain (pain score, whether ongoing pain-relief medication is effective)","Explain that you need to call the doctor to change his/her pain-relief medicine.","Find out if the patient has any other concerns dietician","Encourage the patient to discuss his/her dietary preferences with the hospital"]

ScenarioTitle: Alice, aged 6, was sent to you this morning by her teacher because she had spots on her face.
Background: Alice, aged 6, was sent to you this morning by her teacher because she had spots on her face. After examining her you diagnose chickenpox. You have phoned her parent to ask him/her to come to the school to take Alice home.
TasksJson: ["Explain why you have diagnosed chickenpox (spots on back and arms, some blisters, fever, etc.). Inform the parent of a recent outbreak at Alice\u2019s school.","Emphasise contagious nature of this condition and importance of keeping  Alice at home until no spots can be seen and last blister has completely dried.","Inform parent of usual recovery period (2-3 weeks) and reinforce necessity of staying home during this period.","Outline treatment options (e.g. oral antihistamines, calamine lotion, Zovirax [antiviral drug ], etc.).","Stress that it is important to report any unusual symptoms to a doctor (e.g. sensitivity to light, fever worsening, dehydration, severe headache, etc.)."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is 55 years old and has just had a cerebral angiogram to screen for a brain aneurysm.
Background: Your patient is 55 years old and has just had a cerebral angiogram to screen for a brain aneurysm. He/she has just been transferred to the recovery area before discharge. You are seeing him/her to do clinical observations.
TasksJson: ["Confirm reason for seeing patient (clinical observations). Remind patient of recovery process (e.g., lying still for 2\u20136 hours, gentle mobilisation 4\u20136 hours, monitored by nursing staff, discharge if no concerns, etc.). Find out any other questions/concerns.","Emphasise when food to be available (e.g., when sitting up: avoiding risk of choking/nausea, etc.). Advise need for increased fluid intake before food (e.g., flushing out contrast medium, keeping hydrated, etc.).","Stress need to use bedpan (e.g., provided/taken away by nurse, assistance as required, etc.).","Reassure patient about assistance with bedpan (e.g., your role: all aspects of patient care; no need for embarrassment; etc.). Establish patient\u0027s consent for clinical observations."]

ScenarioTitle: The client has high blood pressure and has been referred to you for advice on lifestyle changes aimed at reducing it.
Background: The client has high blood pressure and has been referred to you for advice on lifestyle changes aimed at reducing it. The medical report indicates that the client smokes, drinks and does not take any regular exercise. He/she has a stressful job as a lawyer.
TasksJson: ["Question the client about his/her smoking, drinking and exercise habits.","Suggest ways in which your client can modify his/her lifestyle to improve his/her health.","Be sympathetic to your client\u0027s reasons for being reluctant to change his/her habits but insist that at least some changes are necessary for the sake of his/her health."]

ScenarioTitle: Your patient is a 22-year-old legal assistant and has had nasal polypectomy surgery.
Background: Your patient is a 22-year-old legal assistant and has had nasal polypectomy surgery. He/she is ready to be discharged. You are seeing him/her to give information about aftercare.
TasksJson: ["Give reason for seeing patient (information on aftercare). Find out how patient is feeling (e.g., any headaches, dizziness, nausea, pain, etc.).","Confirm patient ready for discharge (e.g., clinical observations satisfactory, no further medical attention required, etc.). Advise on wound care (e.g., change dressing every 12 hours/as needed, etc.). Recommend medication for pain relief (e.g., paracetamol/acetaminophen, etc.).","Advise patient nasal drops ready (e.g., from hospital pharmacy, for collection or discharge, etc.).
